questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a parcel of land in fee simple. Five years ago, he conveyed the parcel by deed "to my daughter until she graduates from college, and then to my son in fee simple if he turns 21." The daughter has just graduated from college. The son is only 18 years old.
Who is entitled to possession of the land?

choices.A: The daughter, because she is entitled to possession until her interest is divested by the son's shifting executory interest.
choices.B: The man, because his fee simple interest has not yet been divested by the son's shifting executory interest.
choices.C: The man, because his fee simple interest has not yet been divested by the son's springing executory interest.
choices.D: The son, because his remainder vested when the daughter graduated from college.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible
Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible (Durational)
Fee simple determinable
  • “so long as”
  • “during”
  • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest
(ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Defeasible (Conditional)
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • “but if”
  • “provided that”
  • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

A defeasible fee simple estate is an ownership interest that may last for an indeterminate duration but is limited by specific durational or conditional language (see table above). There are three types of defeasible fees:

  • Fee simple determinable (FSD) — terminates automatically upon the happening of the stated event, then ownership returns to the grantor
  • Fee simple subject to a condition subsequent (FSSCS) — upon the occurrence of a specific condition, the grantor has the right to terminate the estate
  • Fee simple subject to an executory limitation (FSSEL) — upon the occurrence of the stated event or condition, title passes to a third party (ie, someone other than the grantor or the holder of the present fee)

Here, the man conveyed the parcel to his daughter until she graduated from college. This durational language (“until”) means that the daughter received an FSD or FSSEL. The deed then states that, upon her college graduation, the parcel will go to the son if he turns 21. Since title will pass to the son (third party), the daughter received an FSSEL and the son holds an executory interest.

There are two types of executory interests:

  • Shifting — divests the grantee’s estate, such that the estate shifts from the grantee to the executory-interest holder
  • Springing — divests the grantor’s estate, such that the estate springs from the grantor to the executory-interest holder

Here, the daughter’s interest was divested when she graduated from college (Choice A). But since the son is not yet 21, the estate reverted back to the man (grantor).†

This means that the man currently holds an FSD in the parcel — and is therefore entitled to possession — until the son meets the condition of turning 21. Once he turns 21, the parcel will spring from the man to the son, who holds a springing executory interest (Choices B & D).

†Had the son been at least 21 when the daughter graduated from college, the estate would have shifted (not sprung) to the son upon her graduation.

📌 Educational Objective

A shifting executory interest arises when title shifts from the grantee to a third party, while a springing executory interest arises when title springs from the grantor to a third party.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子以完全所有权(fee simple)拥有一块土地。五年前，他通过契据将该地块转让，规定“给我女儿，直到她大学毕业，然后如果我儿子年满21岁，则将完全所有权(fee simple)转让给他。”女儿刚刚大学毕业。儿子只有18岁。

谁有权占有这块土地？

zh-choices.A: 女儿，因为她有权占有该土地，直到她的权益被儿子的转移型未来执行权益(shifting executory interest)所剥夺。
zh-choices.B: 该男子，因为他的完全所有权权益(fee simple interest)尚未被儿子的转移型未来执行权益(shifting executory interest)所剥夺。
zh-choices.C: 该男子，因为他的完全所有权权益(fee simple interest)尚未被儿子的触发型未来执行权益(springing executory interest)所剥夺。
zh-choices.D: 儿子，因为他的剩余权益(remainder)在女儿大学毕业时已既定归属。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：未来权益与占有权

本题考察的是不动产法中关于可废止地产 (Defeasible Fees) 和 未来执行权益 (Executory Interests) 的核心规则，特别是“时间空档”导致的所有权归属问题。

正确答案：C
该男子（父亲）有权占有，因为他的完全所有权权益尚未被儿子的触发型未来执行权益 (Springing Executory Interest) 所剥夺。

逻辑推演图解

初始转让
父亲转让给女儿，条件是“直到大学毕业”。
Fee Simple Determinable
事件发生：女儿毕业
女儿的权益自动终止。此时儿子仅18岁，未满足“年满21岁”的条件。
当前状态：空档期 (The Gap)
谁持有土地？
由于女儿权益结束，儿子权益尚未开始，土地复归 (Revert) 给父亲。
未来展望：儿子满21岁
届时，儿子的权益将从父亲手中夺取所有权。
Springing Executory Interest

核心法律概念解析

1. 自动终止 (Automatic Termination)

契据使用了“直到” (until) 这一期间性用语。这创造了可决定的完全所有权 (Fee Simple Determinable)。当条件（毕业）发生时，女儿的权益立即、自动结束，无需任何法律行动。

2. 填补空档 (Filling the Gap)

这是本题的关键。女儿毕业时，儿子才18岁。法律厌恶所有权的真空。既然儿子还不能接手，所有权必须回到源头。

因此，所有权复归 (Reverts) 给转让人（父亲）。父亲现在拥有土地，直到儿子满21岁。

3. 转移型 vs. 触发型 (Shifting vs. Springing)

这是区分选项A、B和C的关键：

  • 转移型 (Shifting)：权益从一个受让人 (Grantee) 转移给另一个受让人。
    例如：如果儿子在女儿毕业时已满21岁，所有权直接从女儿转给儿子。
  • 触发型 (Springing)：权益从转让人 (Grantor) 转移给受让人。
    本案情况：因为出现了空档，土地回到了父亲手中。将来儿子满21岁时，权益将从父亲（转让人）手中“触发”转移给儿子。

选项辨析

  • 选项 A 错误：女儿的权益是“可决定的” (Determinable)，在毕业那一刻即自动终止。她没有权利继续占有直到儿子满21岁。
  • 选项 B 错误：虽然父亲现在拥有土地，但儿子的权益是触发型 (Springing) 而非转移型 (Shifting)，因为将来它是从父亲（转让人）那里切断所有权，而不是从女儿那里。
  • 选项 D 错误：儿子没有获得剩余权益 (Remainder)。剩余权益通常紧随终身地产 (Life Estate) 自然结束后发生。此处是跟随一个可废止的完全所有权，且存在时间间隔，因此是未来执行权益。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧
在做此类题目时，请务必画出时间轴：
  1. 当前持有人的权益何时结束？
  2. 下一个持有人的条件是否已满足？
  3. 如果条件未满足，中间是否存在时间空档 (Gap)？
如果存在空档，所有权通常会回到转让人 (Grantor) 手中。一旦回到转让人手中，第三方的未来权益通常就变成了触发型 (Springing)。

B.text: fee simple interest has not yet been divested

C.text: fee simple interest has not yet been divested

label.zh: 出让人保留的永久产权

reason.zh: 说明在儿子条件满足前出让人为何仍保有占有权。

D.text: when the daughter graduated from college

reason.en: Treats graduation alone as sufficient to vest the son's interest despite his unmet age condition.
reason.zh: 忽视儿子年龄条件未满足，仅因毕业即认为其权益既成。

highlights.text: until she graduates from college

reason.en: The word until creates a defeasible fee subject to executory limitation in the daughter.
reason.zh: “until”用语使女儿取得可废止且受执行性限制的产权。

highlights.text: then to my son in fee simple if he turns 21

label.zh: 向第三人的附条件授予

reason.en: This clause creates the son's executory interest and the age condition controlling when title passes.
reason.zh: 该条款创设儿子的执行性权益及产权转移的年龄条件。

highlights.text: The daughter has just graduated from college

reason.en: Graduation ends the daughter's present estate and triggers analysis of what happens next.
reason.zh: 毕业终止女儿的现时产权，并触发对后续产权归属的分析。

highlights.text: The son is only 18 years old

reason.en: Because the son is under 21, title reverts to the grantor and his interest is springing, not shifting.
reason.zh: 儿子未满21岁，产权回转给出让人，其权益为创设性而非转移性。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man devised land "to my brother and his heirs until my daughter reaches the age of 25, and then to my daughter and her heirs." The daughter was three years old at the time of her father's death.
The applicable jurisdiction continues to adhere to the common law Rule Against Perpetuities.
Which of the following is the most accurate statement of the daughter's interest in the land?

choices.A: She has a possibility of reverter.
choices.B: She has a remainder interest subject to complete divestment.
choices.C: She has a shifting executory interest.
choices.D: She has no interest in the land because of the Rule Against Perpetuities.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Fee simple absolute
(Indefeasible)
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Fee simple determinable
(Defeasible, Durational)
  • “so long as”
  • “during”
  • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest (ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
(Defeasible, Conditional)
  • “but if”
  • “provided that”
  • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

A defeasible fee has the potential to last forever but can be cut short if a specified event or condition occurs. One type of defeasible fee is a fee simple determinable (FSD), which is created with durational language (eg, “to my brother and his heirs until my daughter reaches the age of 25”). The future interest that follows an FSD is either:

  • possibility of reverter — in which case, the estate automatically reverts back to the grantor when the specified event occurs (presumed if not expressly stated)
  • executory interest — in which case, the estate automatically passes to a third party when the stated event occurs (eg, “then to my daughter and her heirs”).†

Therefore, pursuant to the man’s devise, the daughter has an executory interest (Choice A). There are two types of executory interests:

  • Shifting — cuts short (or divests) an estate held by a grantee, such that the estate shifts from the grantee to the executory-interest holder
  • Springing — cuts short an estate held by a grantor, such that the estate springs from the grantor to the executory-interest holder

Since the daughter’s interest will cut short the brother’s (grantee’s) interest in the land, she has a shifting executory interest.

†An FSD followed by an executory limitation is sometimes referred to as a fee simple determinable subject to an executory limitation.

(Choice B) A remainder is a future interest created in a grantee that is capable of becoming a present estate upon the natural expiration of a life estate, fee tail, or term of years (not seen here). The remainder is subject to complete divestment if the occurrence of a condition will eliminate the interest (eg, “then to A, but if A has no children then to B”).

(Choice D) Under the Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP), certain future interests are void if they could vest more than 21 years after the death of some relevant person alive when the interest was created. But here, the daughter’s executory interest does not violate RAP because she will turn 25 (or not) within her own lifetime.

📌 Educational Objective

A third-party grantee’s executory interest is shifting if it divests another grantee’s estate and springing if it divests the grantor’s estate.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 44 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (fee simple determinable).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子遗赠土地，“将土地遗赠给我的兄弟及其继承人，直到我的女儿年满25岁，届时将土地转给我的女儿及其继承人。” 在父亲去世时，女儿年仅三岁。

该适用的司法管辖区继续遵循普通法中的 Rule Against Perpetuities。

以下哪项是关于女儿在该土地上的权益的最准确陈述？

zh-choices.A: 她拥有一项复归可能性权益（possibility of reverter）。
zh-choices.B: 她拥有一项附有完全被剥夺条件的剩余权益（remainder interest subject to complete divestment）。
zh-choices.C: 她拥有一项转移性待继权益（shifting executory interest）。
zh-choices.D: 由于 Rule Against Perpetuities 的规定，她在该土地上没有任何权益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：未来权益

本题考查的核心是不动产未来权益 (Future Interests) 的分类，特别是如何区分“剩余权益” (Remainder) 和“待继权益” (Executory Interest)。

正确答案：C
She has a shifting executory interest.
(她拥有一项转移性待继权益。)

1. 逐步推理逻辑

要解决这个问题，我们需要分析遗嘱中的语言结构：

兄弟
(Brother)
➔
直到女儿25岁
(Condition)
➔
女儿
(Daughter)

第一步：分析兄弟的权益

遗嘱写道："to my brother... until my daughter reaches the age of 25"。

  • 这里的 "until" 是期间性语言 (Durational Language)。
  • 这创造了一个可废止的完全保有地产 (Fee Simple Determinable)。
  • 这意味着兄弟拥有这块地，但如果特定条件发生（女儿满25岁），他的权益将自动终止。

第二步：分析女儿的权益

遗嘱接着写道："...and then to my daughter..."。

  • 当兄弟的权益终止时，土地没有回到原授予人（父亲/遗嘱执行人）手中，而是去了一个第三方 (Third Party)——女儿手中。
  • 在普通法中，如果一项未来权益属于第三方，并且它切断 (Cuts Short) 了前一个受让人的权益，那么它就是待继权益 (Executory Interest)。

2. 核心考点：Shifting vs. Springing

待继权益分为两类，这是MBE常考的细微差别：

类型 定义 本题情况
转移性
Shifting		 从一个受让人 (Grantee) 转移到另一个受让人。切断了前一个受让人的权益。 ✔ 符合
权益从兄弟（受让人）转移给女儿（受让人）。
引发性
Springing		 从授予人 (Grantor) 转移给受让人。切断了授予人的权益。 ✘ 不符合
如果是"To A when he marries"，在结婚前权益保留在授予人手中，这就是Springing。

3. 为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 A (Possibility of Reverter)：
    复归可能性权益只属于授予人 (Grantor)。如果遗嘱只写了给兄弟直到女儿25岁，没写之后给谁，那么父亲的遗产继承人将拥有此权益。但这里明确给了第三方（女儿）。
  • 选项 B (Remainder)：
    剩余权益 (Remainder) 必须“耐心等待”前一个权益自然结束（如终身地产 Life Estate 结束）。它不能“切断”或“缩短”前一个权益。
    口诀：Remainders wait politely; Executory Interests take rudely.
    由于兄弟拥有的是 Fee Simple（虽然是可废止的），它理论上可以永久持续，女儿的权益是强行切断它，所以只能是 Executory Interest。
  • 选项 D (Rule Against Perpetuities, RAP)：
    RAP 要求权益必须在“在世生命 + 21年”内归属 (Vest)。
    这里，女儿就是在世生命 (Life in Being)。她要么在死前满25岁（权益归属），要么死前未满25岁（权益失效）。无论如何，结果都会在她有生之年确定，不会超过 RAP 时限。因此权益有效。

4. 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

识别关键词：

  • 看到 "But if", "Until", "So long as" ➔ 想到 Defeasible Fees (可废止地产)。
  • 如果后面跟着第三方 ➔ 答案通常是 Executory Interest。
  • 如果后面没跟人（默认回原主） ➔ 答案通常是 Possibility of Reverter 或 Right of Entry。
  • 看到 "For life" ➔ 后面跟着的通常是 Remainder。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Classify future interests from durational language

keywords.text: until my daughter reaches the age of 25

reason.en: Creates a fee simple determinable in the brother, not an absolute fee.

reason.zh: 表明在可消灭地产之后由第三人享有的未来权益。

keywords.text: to my brother and his heirs

reason.en: Identifies whose estate the daughter's interest will divest.
reason.zh: 确定女儿权益将剥夺谁的现持有地产。

reason.en: Shows vesting will occur within a life in being for RAP analysis.
reason.zh: 表明权益归属将在在世者有生之年之内发生，用于永续规则分析。

reason.en: Tests whether the daughter's interest is void as too remote.
reason.zh: 检验女儿权益是否因归属过远而无效。

reason.zh: 确立未来权益在立遗嘱人死亡时产生。

reason.en: Misattributes the post-FSD interest to the grantor instead of a third party.
reason.zh: 误将可消灭地产后的权益归于授予人而非第三人。

reason.en: A remainder must follow a life estate, fee tail, or term of years.
reason.zh: 剩余权必须跟随终身地产、限嗣地产或定期地产。

reason.en: Describes a contingent remainder, not an executory interest here.
reason.zh: 描述的是或然剩余权，而非本案的执行性权益。

reason.en: Correctly identifies a third-party interest that divests another grantee.
reason.zh: 正确识别由第三人享有、并剥夺另一受让人地产的执行性权益。

reason.en: Assumes RAP voids an interest that vests within a life in being.
reason.zh: 假设永续规则会使在在世者有生之年之内归属的权益无效。

reason.en: Invites a RAP violation answer when vesting is certain within 21 years.
reason.zh: 在归属可于二十一年内确定发生时，诱导考生选择违反永续规则的答案。

highlights.text: to my brother and his heirs until my daughter reaches the age of 25, and then to my daughter and her heirs

label.zh: 可消灭非限嗣地产加执行性限制

reason.en: The durational grant to the brother plus the follow-on grant to the daughter controls the entire classification.
reason.zh: 对兄弟的期限性授予加上对女儿的后续授予，决定全部权益分类。

highlights.text: until

reason.en: Triggers creation of a fee simple determinable rather than a fee simple absolute.
reason.zh: 触发创设可消灭非限嗣地产，而非绝对非限嗣地产。

highlights.text: then to my daughter and her heirs

reason.en: Creates an executory interest in the daughter instead of a grantor's possibility of reverter.
reason.zh: 在女儿身上创设执行性权益，而非授予人的复归可能性。

highlights.text: The daughter was three years old at the time of her father's death.

reason.en: Shows the daughter is a life in being and will reach 25 within her lifetime.
reason.zh: 表明女儿为在世者，且将于有生之年满二十五岁。

highlights.text: the daughter's interest in the land

reason.en: Frames the task as identifying the nature of the daughter's future interest.
reason.zh: 将问题框定为识别女儿未来权益的性质。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A grantor owned two tracts of land, one of 15 acres and another of 5 acres. The two tracts were a mile apart.
Fifteen years ago, the grantor conveyed the smaller tract to a grantee. The grantor retained the larger tract. The deed to the grantee contained, in addition to proper legal descriptions of both properties and identifications of the parties, the following language: "I, the grantor, bind myself and my heirs and assigns that in the event that the larger tract that I now retain is ever offered for sale, I will notify the grantee and his heirs and assigns in writing, and the grantee and his heirs and assigns shall have the right to purchase the larger tract for its fair market value as determined by a board consisting of three qualified expert independent real estate appraisers."
With appropriate references to the other property and the parties, there followed a reciprocal provision that conferred upon the grantor and her heirs and assigns a similar right to purchase the smaller tract, purportedly binding the grantee and his heirs and assigns.
Ten years ago, a corporation acquired the larger tract from the grantor. At that time, the grantee had no interest in acquiring the larger tract and by an appropriate written document released any interest he or his heirs or assigns might have had in the larger tract.
Last year, the grantee died. The smaller tract passed by the grantee's will to his daughter. She has decided to sell the smaller tract. However, because she believes that the corporation has been a very poor steward of the larger tract, she refuses to sell the smaller tract to the corporation even though she has offered it for sale in the local real estate market.
The corporation has brought an appropriate action for specific performance of the right of first refusal after taking all the necessary preliminary steps in its effort to exercise its right to purchase the smaller tract. The daughter has asserted all possible defenses.
The common law Rule Against Perpetuities is unmodified in the jurisdiction, and there are no applicable statutes.
If the court rules for the daughter, what will be the likely reason?

choices.A: Noncompliance with a right to purchase gives rise to a claim for money damages, but not for specific performance.
choices.B: The grantee's release 10 years ago operates as a waiver regarding any right to purchase that the corporation might have.
choices.C: The provision setting out the right to purchase violates the Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.D: The two tracts of land were not adjacent parcels of real estate, so the right to purchase is in gross and therefore unenforceable.

questions.explanation:
Rule against perpetuities (RAP)
Does grantee have a contingent future interest?
  • Contingent remainder
  • Vested remainder subject to open
  • Executory interest
  • Power of appointment
  • Right of first refusal
  • Option
No
RAP does not apply
Yes
RAP applies
Must vesting event occur within 21 years after creation of interest?
Yes
Interest valid
No
Could interest possibly vest >21 years after validating life ends?
No
Interest valid
Yes
Common law = interest void
Majority rule = wait & see for 90 years

A right of first refusal is a contractual right to purchase property before any other person if the owner later decides to sell. As a result, it is a contingent future interest that is subject to the Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP).

RAP renders such interests void if there is any possibility that they could vest more than 21 years after some relevant life in being at the creation of the interest. Therefore, rights of first refusal almost always violate RAP if they are not set to terminate - either temporally (eg, calendar date) or by referencing a life in being (eg, within 21 years of the grantee's death) - within the perpetuities period.

Here, the corporation seeks to enforce its right of first refusal over the daughter's smaller tract. Since the deed creating this interest references the parties' heirs and assigns without any mention of a termination date, this right of first refusal could be exercised after the perpetuities period. Therefore, the right of first refusal is invalid under RAP, and the court will likely rule for the daughter on this basis.†

†Since this jurisdiction follows the common-law RAP, this right of first refusal is struck ab initio (ie, from the beginning). But had this jurisdiction adopted the majority "wait and see" stance, the right would have been valid since it vested within 90 years of its creation.

(Choice A) Specific performance is available when money damages are inadequate. Since land is considered unique and money damages cannot compensate for the loss of unique property, this remedy is generally available to those with a right to purchase.

(Choice B) The grantee's waiver of his own right of first refusal as to the larger parcel does not waive the corporation's right to purchase the smaller parcel at issue here.

(Choice D) The adjacency of the tracts is irrelevant. Had the right of first refusal been valid, it would have ripened into a right to purchase in gross (ie, in full) when the seller received an offer from a third-party purchaser. And a right to purchase in gross is enforceable if it complies with RAP.

📌 Educational Objective

To comply with the Rule Against Perpetuities, a right of first refusal must be set to vest or fail within the perpetuities period - ie, within 21 years after some relevant life in being at the creation of the interest.

📚 References
  • 61 Am. Jur. 2d Perpetuities and Restraints on Alienation § 5 (2020) (Rule Against Perpetuities).
questions.zh-question:
一位出让人拥有两块土地，一块15英亩，另一块5英亩。这两块土地相距一英里。

十五年前，出让人将较小地块转让给了一位受让人。出让人保留了较大地块。授予受让人的地契中，除了对两处地产的适当法律描述和各方身份的识别外，还包含以下文字：“我，出让人，约束本人及其继承人和受让人，如果我现在保留的较大地块将来被要约出售，我将书面通知受让人及其继承人和受让人，受让人及其继承人和受让人应有权以其公平市价购买该较大地块，该价格由一个包含三名合格、专业、独立的房地产估价师组成的委员会决定。”

在地契中，通过对另一处地产和当事方的适当援引，随附了一项互惠条款，该条款授予出让人及其继承人和受让人购买较小地块的类似权利，意图约束受让人及其继承人和受让人。

十年前，一家公司从出让人处购得了较大地块。当时，受让人无意购买该较大地块，并通过一份适当的书面文件，放弃了他或其继承人或受让人可能对该较大地块拥有的任何权益。

去年，受让人去世。较小地块根据受让人的遗嘱传给了他的女儿。她决定出售该较小地块。然而，由于她认为该公司对较大地块的管理非常糟糕，尽管她已在当地房地产市场上要约出售，但她拒绝将较小地块出售给该公司。

该公司在采取所有必要初步措施以行使其购买较小地块的权利后，已提起适当诉讼，要求对优先购买权进行强制履行。女儿已提出所有可能的抗辩。

该司法管辖区的普通法 Rule Against Perpetuities 未作修改，且没有适用的成文法。

如果法院裁定女儿胜诉，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 不遵守购买权会引起金钱赔偿的请求，但不会引起强制履行的请求。
zh-choices.B: 十年前受让人的放弃行为，构成了对公司可能拥有的任何购买权的豁免。
zh-choices.C: 规定购买权的条款违反了 Rule Against Perpetuities。
zh-choices.D: 这两块土地并非相邻地块，因此购买权是整体权利（in gross），故不可强制执行。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Rule Against Perpetuities
正确答案：C

本题考查的是普通法下最令人头疼的规则之一：永续禁止规则（Rule Against Perpetuities, RAP）在优先购买权（Right of First Refusal）中的应用。

核心法律逻辑
规则回顾 (RAP)：
任何权益（Interest）如果存在一种可能性，即它可能在“在世人（Life in Being）+ 21年”之后才归属（Vest），那么该权益自始无效（Void Ab Initio）。

让我们通过三步逻辑来拆解本案：

1
权益性质识别：
优先购买权（Right of First Refusal）被视为一种附条件的未来权益（Contingent Future Interest）。在普通法下，这种权益必须遵守 RAP。
2
寻找“测量标准”：
题目中的地契将权利赋予了“受让人及其继承人和受让人”（heirs and assigns），并约束出让人及其“继承人和受让人”。
注意：这里没有设定任何时间限制（如“仅在受让人有生之年有效”）。
3
应用 RAP 测试：
问：这个购买权有没有可能在今天活着的任何人去世21年之后才行使？
答：有。
因为地契约束了“继承人和受让人”，这块地可能在100年后才被出售。届时，现在的当事人都已去世超过21年，但优先购买权才刚刚被触发（归属）。
结论： 由于存在这种“超时归属”的可能性，根据未修改的普通法 RAP，该优先购买权条款自始无效。因此，女儿无需遵守该条款，可以直接出售给第三方。
干扰项排除技巧
  • 选项 A (Remedy)：错误。
    虽然通常违约会导致金钱赔偿，但对于土地合同，强制履行（Specific Performance）是标准救济，因为土地被视为独一无二的（Unique）。如果条款有效，公司本可以要求强制履行。
  • 选项 B (Waiver)：错误。
    受让人放弃对“较大地块”的权利，并不影响公司对“较小地块”拥有的权利。这是两个独立的权利，放弃其一不等于放弃全部。
  • 选项 D (In Gross)：错误。
    土地是否相邻（Adjacent）不影响优先购买权的有效性。即使是整体权利（In Gross，即不依附于土地的个人权利），只要符合 RAP，也是可以强制执行的。这里的关键是 RAP，而不是土地位置。
MBE 考试贴士
当你在 MBE 题目中看到：
  1. 优先购买权 (Right of First Refusal) 或 购买期权 (Option to Purchase)；
  2. 且合同语言包含 "heirs and assigns"（意味着永久性）；
  3. 且没有明确的时间截止日期（如“21年内”）；
请立即警惕 RAP 违规。这几乎是 MBE 考查 RAP 的固定套路。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman owned a four-unit apartment building and lived in one of the units. When one of her tenants vacated his apartment, the woman placed an advertisement in the local paper that read as follows: "Large two-bedroom apartment available for rent. White male preferred." The woman's preference was motivated by the fact that she liked to have a mix of tenants of both genders and from various racial and ethnic backgrounds in her building, and of the remaining rented units, one was rented to an African American man and the other to a Pacific Islander woman.
Based upon these facts, which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: The federal Fair Housing Act makes it illegal for the woman to refuse to rent her units to prospective tenants because of their race or gender.
choices.B: The woman's motive absolves her from any liability under the federal Fair Housing Act.
choices.C: There are no violations of any federal laws under these facts.
choices.D: Under the federal Fair Housing Act, the woman was not permitted to state a racial or gender preference in the advertisement.

questions.explanation:
Fair Housing Act
Applicability Prohibits discriminatory actions in sale/renting of dwelling based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, national origin, or familial status—including:
  • refusing bona fide offer
  • discriminating in terms, conditions, privileges, or services of purchase/rental
  • advertising preference for or discrimination against buyer/renter
  • falsely representing dwelling's availability for inspection, sale, or rental
  • inducing sale/renting with discriminatory representations about neighborhood
  • denying reasonable modifications to accommodate handicap at occupant's expense
Exceptions Act does not apply to:
  • religious organizations
  • private clubs that incidentally provide lodging to members
  • familial status for senior housing
  • owner of ≤ 3 single-family dwellings*
  • owner-occupied dwellings with ≤ 4 units*
  • sale/rental of single-family home by private owner
*These exceptions do not apply to discriminatory advertisements or when owner is assisted by a real estate agent, broker, or salesman.

The federal Fair Housing Act (FHA) was enacted to prohibit discrimination in the sale or rental of a dwelling on the basis of race, color, religion, sex/gender, handicap, national origin, or familial status. Under this act, the following discriminatory actions are prohibited:

  • refusing to sell or rent a dwelling after receipt of a bona fide offer
  • discriminating in the terms, conditions, privileges, or services of sale or rental of a dwelling
  • advertising preference or discrimination with respect to buyers or renters
  • falsely representing that a dwelling is unavailable for inspection, sale, or rental
  • inducing, for profit, the sale or rental of a dwelling with discriminatory representations about the neighborhood
  • refusing to permit, at the occupant's expense, reasonable modifications to accommodate a handicap

Although owner-occupied dwellings with up to four units (as seen here) are generally excepted from the FHA, this exception does not apply to advertisements stating a preference for a protected class. The woman's advertised preference for a "white male" renter constitutes race-based and gender-based discrimination. Therefore, the advertisement is not permitted under the FHA ((Choice C)).

(Choice A) The FHA makes it generally illegal to refuse to rent to a prospective tenant based on race, sex/gender, or other protected class. But since the woman is renting an owner-occupied dwelling with four units, she need not comply with this provision.

(Choice B) The FHA applies when a person's actions have a discriminatory intent or discriminatory effect. Therefore, the woman's positive motive does not absolve her of liability under the FHA because her actions have a discriminatory effect.

📌 Educational Objective

The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in the sale or renting of a dwelling on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, handicap, national origin, or familial status. This includes advertisements that indicate any preference or discrimination with respect to buyers or renters.

📚 References
  • Fair Housing Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 3601 et seq.
questions.zh-question:
一名女子拥有一栋四单元的公寓楼，并居住在其中一个单元。当她的一位租户搬离其公寓时，该女子在当地报纸上刊登了一则广告，内容如下：“宽敞两居室公寓出租。白人男性优先。”该女子的偏好是出于她喜欢楼内租户性别多样、种族和族裔背景各异，而在剩下的已出租单元中，一个租给了一名非洲裔美国男性，另一个租给了一名太平洋岛民女性。

根据这些事实，以下哪项陈述是正确的？

zh-choices.A: 联邦《公平住房法》规定，该女子因潜在租户的种族或性别而拒绝向其出租单元是违法的。
zh-choices.B: 该女子的动机免除了她根据联邦《公平住房法》应承担的任何责任。
zh-choices.C: 根据这些事实，不存在违反任何联邦法律的行为。
zh-choices.D: 根据联邦《公平住房法》，该女子不得在广告中声明种族或性别偏好。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Fair Housing Act
⚖️ 核心考点：FHA 的广告禁令

联邦《公平住房法》(Fair Housing Act, FHA) 禁止在住房销售或租赁中进行歧视。虽然某些小业主可以豁免于“禁止歧视行为”的规定，但没有任何人可以豁免于“禁止歧视性广告”的规定。

1. “墨菲太太例外” (Mrs. Murphy Exemption)

FHA 包含一个著名的例外条款，通常被称为“墨菲太太例外”。如果满足以下条件，业主在选择租户时可以进行歧视（即可以拒绝特定种族或性别的人）：

  • 业主自住 (Owner-occupied)
  • 住宅单元数不超过 4 个 (4 units or less)
  • 未使用房地产经纪人 (No broker used)

在本题中，该女子拥有一栋四单元公寓并住在其中，因此她符合这一例外。这意味着，如果她只是私下决定不租给某人，她可能不会违反 FHA（选项 A 错误）。

2. 广告没有例外 (The Advertising Ban)

这是本题的致命陷阱。FHA 第 3604(c) 条明确规定，发布任何表明偏好、限制或歧视的通知、声明或广告都是违法的。

这项规定适用于所有人，包括符合“墨菲太太例外”的业主。即使你有权在心里歧视，你也不能在报纸上大声嚷嚷。

⚠️ 关键区别：
你可以“做”（在特定豁免情况下拒绝租客），但你绝对不能“说”（发布歧视性广告）。
3. 动机无关紧要 (Motive is Irrelevant)

题目中提到该女子的动机是为了“促进多样性”（想要白人男性来平衡现有的非裔和太平洋岛民租户）。

然而，FHA 对歧视性广告的禁令是严格的。无论出于何种善意目的，只要广告内容表明了基于受保护特征（种族、性别等）的偏好，即构成违法。因此，选项 B 错误。

行为 普通房东 本案房东
(自住+4单元以下)
拒绝租客
(基于种族/性别)		 ✘ 违法 ✔ 合法
(FHA例外)
发布广告
(声明偏好)		 ✘ 违法 ✘ 违法
(无例外!)
✅ 正确答案：D

根据联邦《公平住房法》，该女子不得在广告中声明种族或性别偏好。即使她是自住小业主，广告禁令依然适用。

A.text: because of their race or gender

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
In the most recent deed in the chain of title to a tract of land, a man conveyed the land as follows: "To my niece and her heirs and assigns in fee simple until my niece's daughter marries, and then to my niece's daughter and her heirs and assigns in fee simple."
There is no applicable statute, and the common law Rule Against Perpetuities has not been modified in the jurisdiction.
Which of the following is the most accurate statement concerning the title to the land?

choices.A: The niece has a defeasible fee simple determinable and the daughter has an executory interest.
choices.B: The niece has a fee simple and the daughter has no interest, because after the grant of a fee simple there can be no gift over.
choices.C: The niece has a fee simple and the daughter has no interest, because she might not marry within 21 years after the date of the deed.
choices.D: The niece has a life estate and the daughter has a contingent remainder.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible
Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible Fee simple determinable
  • Durational
    • “so long as”
    • “during”
    • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter

Third party’s executory interest (fee simple subject to executory limitation)

Grantor’s right of entry
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • Conditional
    • “but if”
    • “provided that”
    • “unless”

Defeasible fees are fee simple estates that may be terminated by the occurrence of a stated event. One type of defeasible fee is a fee simple determinable (FSD), which is created with durational language (eg, “to my niece until my niece’s daughter marries”). The future interest that follows an FSD is either: a possibility of reverter — in which case, the estate automatically reverts back to the grantor when the stated event occurs (presumed if not expressly stated) or an executory interest — in which case, the estate automatically passes to a third party (grantee) when the stated event occurs (eg, “then to my niece’s daughter”).

Therefore, pursuant to the man’s conveyance, the niece has a defeasible fee simple determinable and the daughter holds an executory interest (Choices B & D).

(Choice C) The Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) renders a future interest void if there is any possibility that it could vest more than 21 years after the death of some relevant person alive when the interest was created. But here, the daughter’s executory interest does not violate RAP because she will marry (or not) within her own lifetime.

📌 Educational Objective

A fee simple determinable (FSD) is a type of defeasible fee that is created with durational language. FSDs can be followed by a grantor’s possibility of reverter OR a third party’s executory interest.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property §§ 44, 47 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing the fee simple determinable and fee simple determinable subject to executory limitation).

questions.zh-question:
在一块土地的产权链（chain of title）中最新的地契（deed）里，一名男子按如下方式转让了该土地：“将土地以 fee simple (完全保有地产权) 的形式转让给我的侄女及其继承人和受让人，直到我侄女的女儿结婚为止，届时再以 fee simple (完全保有地产权) 的形式转让给我侄女的女儿及其继承人和受让人。”

该司法管辖区内没有适用的成文法，且普通法中的 Rule Against Perpetuities (反永久所有权规则) 未被修改。

以下哪项是关于该土地所有权（title）最准确的陈述？

zh-choices.A: 侄女拥有一个 defeasible fee simple determinable (可废止的可决定地产权)，而女儿拥有一个 executory interest (待生效权益)。
zh-choices.B: 侄女拥有一个 fee simple (完全保有地产权)，而女儿没有任何权益，因为在授予 fee simple 之后，不能再有后续的赠与。
zh-choices.C: 侄女拥有一个 fee simple (完全保有地产权)，而女儿没有任何权益，因为她可能不会在地契签订之日起21年内结婚。
zh-choices.D: 侄女拥有一个 life estate (终身地产权)，而女儿拥有一个 contingent remainder (或有剩余地产权)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Future Interests

✅ 正确答案分析 (Choice A)

本题的核心在于识别持续性语言 (Durational Language) 以及随之产生的未来权益 (Future Interest)。

正确结论是：侄女拥有 Fee Simple Determinable，女儿拥有 Executory Interest。

法律推理步骤

1 识别现时权益 (Present Estate)

地契中使用了 "until"（直到...为止）这一词汇。这是典型的持续性语言 (Durational Language)，类似的词还包括 "so long as", "during", "while"。

  • 这种语言创造了一种可自动终止的权益。
  • 因此，侄女拥有的不是绝对的 Fee Simple Absolute，而是一个Defeasible Fee (可废止地产权)，具体为 Fee Simple Determinable。
2 识别未来权益 (Future Interest)

当条件触发（女儿结婚）时，地产权去向何处？

  • 如果是自动回到转让人 (Grantor) 手中，那是 Possibility of Reverter。
  • 但在本题中，地产权转移给了第三方（即女儿）。
  • 当 Fee Simple 被切断并转移给第三方时，该第三方的权益称为 Executory Interest (待生效权益)。
3 RAP 检验 (Rule Against Perpetuities)

MBE 经常考察 Executory Interest 是否违反 RAP。

  • 规则：权益必须在“在世生命 (Life in Being) + 21年”内确定归属或失效。
  • 本案分析：“女儿”是测量生命。她是否结婚，在她自己有生之年（或死时）必然会有定论。
  • 结论：这不可能超过她死后21年才发生，因此不违反 RAP。选项 C 错误。

关键概念对比

Fee Simple Determinable vs. Subject to Condition Subsequent

这是 MBE 必考的区别：

1. Determinable (本题):
"Until", "So long as"
➔ 自动终止 (Automatic forfeiture)。

2. Condition Subsequent:
"But if", "Provided that"
➔ 不会自动终止，转让人必须行使 Right of Entry。

Executory Interest vs. Remainder

Remainder (剩余地产权):
耐心等待前一个地产权（通常是 Life Estate）自然结束。

Executory Interest (待生效权益):
粗鲁地切断 (Cut short) 前一个地产权（通常是 Fee Simple）。本题中，女儿的权益切断了侄女的权益，所以是 Executory Interest。

为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 B: 错误地认为 Fee Simple 后不能有赠与。法律允许 Defeasible Fee，即附带条件的 Fee Simple。
  • 选项 C: 错误地应用了 RAP。如上所述，女儿的结婚与否在她有生之年必见分晓，不会违反规则。
  • 选项 D: 错误地将其定性为 Life Estate。虽然侄女可能只拥有一辈子（如果女儿一直不结婚），但措辞是 "heirs and assigns" 且以事件（结婚）为界限，这在法律上被归类为 Fee Simple Determinable，而非 Life Estate。
MBE Property 备考要点：看到 "Until/So long as" 先想 Determinable；看到第三方先想 Executory Interest。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
By a writing, a homeowner leased his home to a law student for a term of three years, ending December 31 of last year, at the rent of $1,000 per month. The lease provided that the law student could sublet and assign.
The law student lived in the home for one year and paid the rent promptly. After one year, he leased the home to a graduate student for one year at a rent of $1,000 per month.
The graduate student took possession of the home and lived there for six months but, because of her unemployment, paid no rent. After six months, on June 30, the graduate student abandoned the home, which remained vacant for the balance of that year. The law student again took possession of the home at the beginning of the third and final year of the term but paid the homeowner no rent.
At the end of the lease term, the homeowner brought an appropriate action against both the law student and the graduate student to recover $24,000, the unpaid rent.
In such action, the homeowner is entitled to a judgment against whom?

choices.A: The law student individually for $12,000, and against the law student and graduate student jointly and severally for $12,000.
choices.B: The law student individually for $18,000, and against the law student and graduate student jointly and severally for $6,000.
choices.C: The law student individually for $18,000, and against the graduate student individually for $6,000.
choices.D: The law student individually for $24,000, and no judgment against the graduate student.

questions.explanation:
Privity with landlord

Sublease
Homeowner
→
Law student
→
Graduate student
→
Law student
→
Homeowner
Privity of contract & estate
 
Privity of contract & estate

A landlord and tenant have a legal relationship based on both:

  • privity of contract – their shared interest in the lease agreement and
  • privity of estate – the landlord's successive right to possess the property (ie, the tenant's current right of possession is immediately followed by the landlord's future right of possession).

Unless the lease states otherwise, either party can freely transfer his/her interest under the lease. Subletting is a partial transfer of a tenant's interest to a third party (sublessee) for less than the remainder of the tenant's lease term. Despite that transfer, a sublessee is not liable to the landlord for a breach of the lease because:

  • no lease agreement exists between the landlord and the sublessee (no privity of contract) and
  • the original tenant will regain possession of the property before the landlord does (no privity of estate).

Therefore, the original tenant is individually liable for the landlord's entire harm arising from a breach of the lease by the sublessee.

Here, the homeowner leased his home to the law student for three years at $1,000 per month. After one year, the law student sublet the home to a graduate student for one year (less than the remainder of the lease). Since the graduate student was a sublessee (no privity with homeowner), she is not liable to the homeowner. However, the law student—the original tenant—is individually liable for the homeowner's entire harm arising from a breach of the lease (Choices A, B & C). And since no rent was paid for the final two years of the lease (breach), the homeowner is entitled to a judgment against the law student for the full amount ($24,000).

📌 Educational Objective

A tenant who sublets—ie, transfers his/her interest to a third party (sublessee) for less than the remainder of the lease term—is individually liable for the landlord's entire harm arising from a breach of the lease by the sublessee. However, the sublessee has no liability to the landlord.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 15.1 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (right to transfer lease interest).
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 16.1 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (tenant remains liable after sublet based on privity of contract and privity of estate).
questions.zh-question:
一名房主以书面形式将其房屋出租给一名法学院学生，租期三年，于去年12月31日到期，月租金为1000美元。租赁合同规定，该法学院学生可以分租和转让。

该法学院学生在该房屋居住了一年，并按时支付了租金。一年后，他以每月1000美元的租金将该房屋租给一名研究生，租期为一年。

该研究生占有了该房屋并居住了六个月，但由于失业，未支付任何租金。六个月后，即6月30日，该研究生弃置了该房屋，该房屋在该年度剩余时间内一直空置。在租期的第三年即最后一年开始时，该法学院学生再次占有该房屋，但未向房主支付任何租金。

租期结束时，房主对法学院学生和研究生提起适当的诉讼，要求追讨24000美元的未付租金。

在此诉讼中，房主有权获得对谁的判决？

zh-choices.A: 法学院学生个人承担12000美元，法学院学生和研究生对另外12000美元承担连带责任。
zh-choices.B: 法学院学生个人承担18000美元，法学院学生和研究生对另外6000美元承担连带责任。
zh-choices.C: 法学院学生个人承担18000美元，研究生个人承担6000美元。
zh-choices.D: 法学院学生个人承担24000美元，且对研究生无判决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Landlord & Tenant
核心考点：分租 vs. 转让

本题的关键在于判断法学院学生（T1）与研究生（T2）之间的交易是 Assignment (转让) 还是 Sublease (分租)。

租赁期时间线图解：

第1年 T1 居住
第2年 T2 (分租)
第3年 T1 (收回)

1. 法律定性：Sublease (分租)

规则：如果原承租人转让的时间短于其剩余的租赁期限，并保留了Reversionary Interest (回复权)，则该转让为 Sublease。

本案分析：T1 的租期还剩2年，但他只租给 T2 1年。T1 保留了第3年的占有权（事实上他也确实在第3年搬回去了）。因此，这是一个 Sublease。

2. 责任分析：Privity (债的关联)

房主 (L) 能否起诉某人，取决于他们之间是否存在以下两种关系之一：

  • Privity of Contract (合同之债)： 双方是否签署了合同？
  • Privity of Estate (财产之债/地产关联)： 双方是否在土地占有上存在直接的法律链条？

对法学院学生 (T1) 的分析：

  • 合同关系：有。T1 与房主签署了原始租约。除非房主明确释放 (Release/Novation)，否则 T1 始终承担支付租金的合同义务。
  • 结论：T1 对全部未付租金 ($24,000) 负责。

对研究生 (T2) 的分析：

  • 合同关系：无。T2 只与 T1 签了合同，没与房主签。
  • 地产关联 (Privity of Estate)：无。这是 Sublease 的核心特征。在 Sublease 中，T1 保留了部分权益，隔断了房主与 T2 之间的地产关联。
  • 结论：T2 对房主不承担任何直接责任。

注：如果是 Assignment (转让全部剩余租期)，T2 将与房主建立 Privity of Estate，从而需要承担责任。但本题是 Sublease。

✅ 正确答案：D

法学院学生个人承担 $24,000，对研究生无判决。

因为是 Sublease，次承租人 (Sublessee) 对原房主既无合同义务也无地产义务。原承租人 (Original Tenant) 始终因合同关系对房主负全责。

MBE Property Law Review © 2025

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An elderly man and a landlord entered into a one-year agreement to lease a one-bedroom apartment. Six months into the lease, the man accidentally fell down a flight of stairs and broke his hip. As a result, he was no longer able to care for himself, and his family moved him into a nursing home. The man ceased paying rent for the next two months. When the landlord finally reached the man at the nursing home, the man informed the landlord that he had left the apartment two months earlier and did not intend to return. The landlord notified the man that he did not accept the man's abandonment of the lease, and for the remaining four months of the lease, the landlord did not take any steps to re-rent the abandoned apartment despite receiving multiple inquiries about the apartment.
The landlord has sued the man for breach of contract to recover damages for unpaid rent.
What amount of damages will the court likely hold the man liable for?

choices.A: Two months' rent, because the man is not liable for future rent after he provided notice of abandonment to the landlord.
choices.B: Four months' rent, because the landlord affirmatively rejected the man's abandonment of the lease.
choices.C: Six months' rent, because the landlord did not have a duty to mitigate damages upon the man's unjustifiable abandonment.
choices.D: None, because the man's abandonment of the lease was justifiable due to necessity.

questions.explanation:
Unjustifiable abandonment of leased property

Offer to surrender rights
  • Tenant abandoned leased property
  • with intent to terminate lease without legal justification (eg, by refusing to pay rent)
Offer accepted
  • By landlord's express agreement
  • By landlord retaking possession of property plus either:
    • landlord's own use of property
    • re-renting property to third party
▼
Lease terminated
Tenant not liable for future rent
Offer rejected
▼
Lease continues
Tenant liable for future rent
▼
Duty to mitigate damages
  • Majority rule: landlord must make reasonable effort to re-rent property
  • Minority rule: no duty to mitigate

A tenant's unjustifiable abandonment of leased property is treated as an offer to surrender rights under the lease. The landlord can then accept or reject the tenant's offer. If the offer is rejected, the lease continues and the tenant must continue paying rent. However, in a majority of jurisdictions, the landlord has a duty to mitigate damages by making a reasonable effort to re-rent the property.† If the landlord fails to do so, then the landlord's damages will be reduced by what the landlord could have reasonably received by re-renting the property.

Here, the man stopped paying rent for two months before informing the landlord that he had abandoned the leased apartment. Although the man abandoned the lease because of his medical needs, a tenant's personal circumstances rarely justify abandonment (Choice D). Therefore, the man is liable for those two months of unpaid rent.

The landlord then rejected the man's offer to surrender his rights under the lease, so the man remained obligated to pay rent for the four months left under the lease. But since the landlord failed to take any steps to re-rent the apartment pursuant to his duty to mitigate damages—even after receiving multiple inquiries about the apartment—the court will likely find that the man is not liable for the remaining four months of rent (Choices B & C).

†A landlord who re-rents the premises for less than the price in the lease may hold the tenant liable for any deficiency.

📌 Educational Objective

If a landlord rejects a tenant's offer of abandonment, the tenant is obligated to pay rent for the remainder of the lease. However, in most jurisdictions, a landlord has a duty to mitigate damages by making a reasonable effort to re-rent the property and the tenant's liability for rent will be reduced accordingly.

📚 References
  • 49 Am. Jur. 2d Landlord & Tenant § 609 (2020) (discussing a landlord's duty to mitigate damages).
questions.zh-question:
一名年迈的男子与一位房东签订了一份为期一年的一居室公寓租赁协议。租约开始六个月后，该男子意外从楼梯上摔下，摔断了髋骨。因此，他无法再照顾自己，其家人将他送入了一家养老院。在接下来的两个月里，该男子停止支付租金。当房东最终在养老院联系到该男子时，该男子告知房东他已于两个月前离开公寓，并且不打算返回。房东通知该男子，他不接受其放弃租约的行为，并且在租约剩余的四个月里，尽管收到了多个关于该公寓的问询，房东未采取任何措施重新出租该已废弃的公寓。

房东已就违约起诉该男子，要求赔偿未付的租金损失。

法院可能判决该男子承担多少金额的损害赔偿责任？

zh-choices.A: 两个月的租金，因为在该男子向房东发出放弃租约的通知后，他无需对未来的租金负责。
zh-choices.B: 四个月的租金，因为房东明确拒绝了该男子放弃租约的行为。
zh-choices.C: 六个月的租金，因为在该男子无理放弃租约的情况下，房东没有减轻损害的义务。
zh-choices.D: 无，因为该男子因紧急避险而放弃租约是正当的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Landlord-Tenant Law
核心考点：减轻损害义务

在大多数司法管辖区（Modern Majority Rule），当承租人无理弃租（Abandonment）时，房东有义务减轻损害 (Duty to Mitigate Damages)。

这意味着房东必须做出合理的努力 (Reasonable Effort) 重新出租房屋。如果房东未能履行此义务，其可获得的赔偿将扣除其本可以通过重新出租获得的金额。

📅 案情时间轴分析

第 1-6 个月
租约正常履行。
第 7-8 个月 (关键点1)
租客停止付租金，但未通知房东。房东不知情，无法采取行动。
➡ 租客需赔偿这2个月租金。
第 9-12 个月 (关键点2)
房东得知弃租。尽管有人询问，房东未采取任何措施重新出租。
➡ 房东违反减轻损害义务，无法追讨这4个月租金。
正确答案：选项 A

为什么是两个月？

法院的判决逻辑分为两部分：

  1. 前两个月： 租客虽然搬走了，但没有通知房东。房东在不知情的情况下无法去寻找新租客（无法减轻损害）。因此，租客必须支付这段时间的租金。
  2. 后四个月： 房东明确知道租客弃租。根据减轻损害义务 (Duty to Mitigate)，房东不能任由房屋空置来积累损失。题目明确指出房东“未采取任何措施”且“无视了多次问询”。因此，法律视作房东本可以把房子租出去，这部分的损失是房东自己造成的，租客无需赔偿。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 B (四个月) / C (六个月)

这两个选项基于旧的普通法规则 (Common Law Rule)，即房东没有减轻损害的义务。但在MBE考试中，除非另有说明，通常适用现代多数规则，即房东必须尝试减轻损害。

选项 D (无责任)

虽然租客是因为健康原因（摔断髋骨）搬走，但这属于个人不幸，并不构成合同法上的“紧急避险” (Necessity) 或“履行不能” (Impossibility) 来免除支付租金的合同义务。个人困难通常不能作为违约的正当理由。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Abandonment" (弃租) 和 "Landlord does nothing" (房东不作为) 的组合时，立刻联想 Duty to Mitigate。

如果题目说房东尝试了但没租出去（Reasonable Effort），租客仍需负责；但如果房东完全躺平（No steps taken），租客的责任通常会被免除。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A son loaned his father a large sum of money. The father signed a 10-year promissory note and secured the note with a mortgage on his farm. The mortgage was promptly recorded.
The next year, the father died intestate. The father's heirs were the son and his two sisters. The sisters first learned of the mortgage just after their father died.
The sisters now assert that the son, their brother, holds the mortgage for their benefit as well as for himself because as a tenant in common with his sisters, he has a fiduciary duty toward them.
There are no applicable statutes.
Are the sisters correct?

choices.A: No, because the mortgage was granted before the tenancy in common was created.
choices.B: No, because the three siblings took the farm as tenants in common rather than as joint tenants with right of survivorship.
choices.C: Yes, because a fiduciary relationship exists among tenants in common.
choices.D: Yes, because their three interests are equal.

questions.explanation:
Father owns farm
Son acquires mortgage on farm
Son acquires mortgage on farm
Siblings inherit farm as tenants in common
Siblings inherit farm as tenants in common
Fiduciary relationship

Son holds mortgage for his benefit only

Siblings inherit farm as tenants in common
Siblings inherit farm as tenants in common
Son acquires mortgage on farm
Son acquires mortgage on farm
Fiduciary relationship

Son holds mortgage for cotenants' benefit

Cotenants generally do not share a fiduciary relationship unless they become cotenants at the same time. The fiduciary relationship exists only with respect to transactions taking place during the tenancy. (Choice C)

When the mortgage was granted before the siblings inherited the farm, the son does not have a fiduciary duty to the siblings.

(Choice B) The outcome would be the same even if the siblings were joint tenants with right of survivorship.

(Choice D) Although the siblings' interests are presumed equal in intestate succession, that does not affect the outcome of this dispute.

📌 Educational Objective

Cotenants share a fiduciary relationship if they become cotenants at the same time. But this fiduciary relationship exists only with respect to transactions that occur during the tenancy.
questions.zh-question:
一个儿子借给他的父亲一大笔钱。父亲签署了一份为期10年的本票，并以其农场设立抵押来担保该本票。该抵押权被及时登记。

第二年，父亲无遗嘱去世。父亲的继承人是儿子和他的两个姐妹。姐妹们在父亲去世后才得知该抵押权的存在。

姐妹们现在主张，她们的兄弟，即那个儿子，持有该抵押权是为了她们和他自己的共同利益，因为作为与她们的按份共有人，他对她们负有信托责任。

没有适用的成文法。

姐妹们的说法正确吗？

zh-choices.A: 不正确，因为该抵押权的授予时间早于按份共有关系的建立时间。
zh-choices.B: 不正确，因为三兄妹是以按份共有人的身份继承农场，而非带遗属权的联权共有人。
zh-choices.C: 正确，因为按份共有人之间存在信托关系。
zh-choices.D: 正确，因为他们三人的权益是相等的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Cotenancy & Fiduciary Duties

正确答案：A

核心理由：抵押权是在共有关系（Cotenancy）建立之前就已经存在的。

虽然共有人之间通常存在信托责任，但这种责任不适用于在成为共有人之前就已经获得的权益。

时间线分析 (Timeline Analysis)

解决本题的关键在于理清事件发生的先后顺序：

第一阶段 (Year 1)
儿子借钱给父亲，获得抵押权 (Mortgage)。
此时双方是债权人与债务人关系。
第二阶段 (Year 2)
父亲去世，兄妹三人继承农场。
此时按份共有 (Tenancy in Common) 关系建立。
争议点 (Current)
姐妹要求分享抵押权利益。
关键点：信托责任 (Fiduciary Duty) 仅适用于共有关系存续期间发生的交易。
法律规则详解 (Legal Principles)

1. 一般规则 (General Rule)：
共有人（无论是 Tenants in Common 还是 Joint Tenants）之间通常不具有信托关系 (Fiduciary Relationship)。他们通常可以像陌生人一样通过公平交易买卖彼此的份额。

2. 例外情况 (The Exception)：
如果共有人是通过同一份遗嘱或继承（如本案）同时获得产权的，法院通常会认定他们之间存在信托关系。这意味着，如果其中一人购买了该房产上的未偿留置权 (Outstanding Title or Lien)（例如买下法拍房或欠税留置权），法律会推定他是为了所有共有人的利益购买的。

条件是：其他共有人必须在合理时间内支付其应分担的费用。

3. 例外的例外 (本题考点)：
上述信托责任不适用于共有人在成为共有人之前就已经拥有的权益。在本案中，儿子在父亲去世前（即共有关系建立前）就已经合法拥有了该抵押权。他作为“债权人”的身份早于他作为“共有人”的身份。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 C (干扰性最强)：
它正确地指出了共有人之间可能存在信托关系，但忽略了时间性这一关键要素。如果儿子是在父亲去世后，从银行买下了父亲原本欠银行的抵押贷款，那么选项 C 可能是正确的。

❌ 选项 B：
共有形式是 Tenants in Common 还是 Joint Tenants 与本题无关。无论哪种形式，关于“先前存在的权益”的规则是一样的。

❌ 选项 D：
份额相等 (Equal Interests) 是无遗嘱继承的默认规则，但这并不产生要求分享个人私有财产（抵押权）的法律义务。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理不动产 (Real Property) 题目时，务必画出时间轴。很多法律后果（如抵押权的优先顺位、信托责任的产生、契约的合并）都完全取决于事件发生的先后顺序。

看到 "Before" 和 "After" 这类时间词汇时，要格外警惕。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Twenty years ago, the owner of a one-acre tract of land duly delivered a deed of the land "to the school district so long as it is used for school purposes." The deed was promptly and properly recorded. Five years ago, the owner died, leaving a son as his only heir; however, by his duly probated will, he left "all my estate to my friend."
Last month, the school district closed its school on the land and for valid consideration duly executed and delivered a quitclaim deed of the land to a developer, who planned to use the land for commercial development. The developer has now brought an appropriate action to quiet title against the son, the friend, and the school district.
The only applicable statute is a provision in the jurisdiction's probate code which provides that any property interest that is descendible is devisable.
In such action, the court should find that title is now in whom?

choices.A: The developer.
choices.B: The friend.
choices.C: The school district.
choices.D: The son.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible Fee simple determinable
  • Durational
    • “so long as”
    • “during”
    • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest
(ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • Conditional
    • “but if”
    • “provided that”
    • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

A fee simple determinable (FSD) is created with durational language (eg, “until”) and automatically terminates upon the happening of a specified event or condition (eg, when land is no longer used for school purposes). An FSD is followed by either:

  • a possibility of reverter – when the estate automatically reverts back to the grantor upon the happening of the specified event (presumed if not expressly stated) or
  • an executory interest – when the estate automatically passes to a third party upon the happening of the specified event (must be expressly stated).

Both these future interests are freely transferable during life, devisable by will, and descendible by inheritance.

Here, the deed conveyed created an FSD in the school district and a possibility of reverter in the owner. The owner devised all of his estate – including the possibility of reverter – to the friend, leaving no interest for the son to inherit upon the owner’s death (Choice D). And since the school district’s estate automatically terminated when it closed the school, it had nothing to convey to the developer in the quitclaim deed (Choices A & C). Instead, title to the land automatically transferred to the friend, the reversionary interest holder.

📌 Educational Objective

A fee simple determinable is followed by either a possibility of reverter (if it reverts to the grantor) or an executory interest (if it passes to a third party). Both future interests are freely transferable during life, devisable by will, and descendible by inheritance.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property §§ 159, 164–65 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (transferability of reversionary interests).
questions.zh-question:
二十年前，一处一英亩土地的所有人正式交付了一份土地契约，“只要该土地用于学校目的，就归于学区。” 该契约被及时且适当地登记了。五年前，该所有人去世，留下一个儿子作为其唯一继承人；然而，在他经过正式遗嘱检验的遗嘱中，他将“我的所有财产”留给了他的朋友。

上个月，学区关闭了其在该土地上的学校，并为了有效的对价，正式签署并向一个开发商交付了该土地的免责契约，该开发商计划将该土地用于商业开发。该开发商现已对该儿子、朋友及学区提起了适当的确认产权诉讼。

唯一适用的法条是该司法管辖区遗嘱检验法典中的一项规定，该规定指出任何可被继承的财产权益也是可被遗赠的。

在此诉讼中，法院应裁定该土地的所有权现在归谁所有？

zh-choices.A: 开发商。
zh-choices.B: 朋友。
zh-choices.C: 学区。
zh-choices.D: 儿子。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Real Property: Future Interests

核心考点 本题考察的是附确定期限的完全保有地产 (Fee Simple Determinable) 及其对应的未来权益——复归可能性 (Possibility of Reverter) 的性质与转移。
1识别地产类型

契约中的用语 "so long as it is used for school purposes"（只要用于学校目的）是典型的持续性语言 (Durational Language)。

这种语言创造了 Fee Simple Determinable (FSD)。其特点是：一旦条件被打破，地产权自动 (Automatically) 终止，无需原所有人采取任何法律行动。

类型 关键用语 终止方式
FSD
(本题)		 So long as,
Until,
During		 自动终止
(Automatic)
FSSCS
(条件后续)		 But if,
Provided that		 需行使进入权
(Right of Entry)
2确定未来权益归属

当所有人设立 FSD 时，他保留了 Possibility of Reverter (复归可能性)。这是一种未来权益。

题目中的法条指出："descendible"（可继承的）权益也是 "devisable"（可遗赠的）。

关键推理链条：

所有人 (Owner)
持有 Possibility of Reverter
↓ 去世 (遗嘱)
朋友 (Friend)
通过遗嘱获得 "all my estate"
(包含复归可能性)
↓ 学校关闭
朋友 (Friend)
自动获得 Fee Simple Absolute
(土地所有权)
3分析当前状态

当学区关闭学校时，"用于学校目的" 的条件不再满足。由于是 FSD，学区的权利瞬间自动终止。

此时，土地所有权立即回到了复归可能性的持有人手中。根据遗嘱，这个持有人是朋友。

因此，学区随后签发给开发商的免责契约 (Quitclaim Deed) 是无效的，因为那时学区已经没有任何权利可以转让了。

正确答案：B (The friend)

为什么其他选项是错的？

A. The Developer (开发商)
错误。开发商从学区购买土地时，学区的权利已经因为学校关闭而自动终止了。学区不能转让它不拥有的东西 (Nemo dat quod non habet)。
C. The School District (学区)
错误。FSD 的性质决定了违反条件时权利自动丧失，不会停留在学区手中。
D. The Son (儿子)
错误。虽然儿子是法定继承人 (Heir)，但所有人留下了有效的遗嘱 (Will)，将所有财产给了朋友。遗嘱优先于法定继承。Possibility of Reverter 是可以通过遗嘱转让的财产权益。
💡 MBE 提分技巧
在做此类题目时，务必区分 Fee Simple Determinable (FSD) 和 Fee Simple Subject to Condition Subsequent (FSSCS)。

如果是 FSSCS（例如用词是 "but if"），违反条件不会自动终止权利，必须由持有 "Right of Entry" 的人采取行动收回。如果本题是 FSSCS，且朋友未行使权利，学区（及开发商）可能仍持有土地。但本题是 "so long as" (FSD)，所以是自动回归。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An elderly woman owned a large manor in fee simple. Because of her advanced age, she no longer wished to deal with maintenance and other obligations associated with homeownership. She therefore conveyed the manor to her eldest son for life, remainder to her youngest son.
The youngest son took ill and died three years later, leaving his entire estate to a friend under the terms of his duly executed will. The youngest son was survived by his daughter, his sole heir. The eldest son died six months later, survived by the elderly woman, the friend, and the daughter.
The jurisdiction in which the manor is situated recognizes traditional common-law rules regarding the destructibility of contingent remainders.
In an appropriate action between the elderly woman, the friend, and the daughter to determine title to the manor, who will prevail?

choices.A: The daughter, because she is the youngest son's heir.
choices.B: The elderly woman, because she had a reversion that entitled her to possession of the manor immediately upon the eldest son's death.
choices.C: The elderly woman, because the youngest son's contingent remainder was destroyed when he predeceased the eldest son.
choices.D: The friend, because the youngest son's vested remainder was transferred by his will.

questions.explanation:
grantor ↓
life tenant ↓
remainderman ↓

The elderly woman conveyed the manor to her eldest son for life, remainder to her youngest son.

Life estate
(present estate)
Vested remainder
(future interest)

A life estate is a present possessory interest in real property that terminates on the death of an individual. The future interest that follows a life estate is either a reversion (if held by the grantor) or a remainder (if created in a grantee – as seen here). Remainders are either:

  • vested – not subject to any condition precedent AND held by an identifiable living person (eg, “remainder to my youngest son”) or
  • contingent – subject to a condition precedent OR held by an unknown or unborn person (eg, “remainder to my youngest son, but only if …”).

Both types of remainders are fully transferable during the grantee’s lifetime,† devisable by will, and inheritable through intestate succession.

Here, the elderly woman conveyed the manor to her eldest son for life, remainder to her youngest son. Since the manor would go to the youngest son unconditionally when the eldest son died, the youngest son had a vested remainder. That remainder was devisable, so it transferred to his friend under the terms of his duly executed will. And since the eldest son has since died, the friend has title to the manor in fee simple.

†At common law and in a minority of jurisdictions, contingent remainders are not transferable during the grantee’s lifetime.

(Choice A) The daughter has no interest in the manor because the youngest son devised his vested remainder to the friend.

(Choice B) The elderly woman (grantor) did not have a reversion that entitled her to possession immediately upon the eldest son’s death. Instead, the friend was entitled to possession of the manor at that time because he had the youngest son’s remainder interest.

(Choice C) At common law and in this jurisdiction, contingent remainders are destroyed if they have not vested by the time the prior estate terminates. But this rule does not affect the youngest son’s vested remainder.

📌 Educational Objective

Remainders—whether they are vested or contingent—are fully transferable during the grantee’s lifetime, devisable by will, and inheritable through intestate succession.

📚 References
  • Moore v. McKinley, 69 N.W.2d 73, 80 (Iowa 1955) (describing the difference between vested and contingent remainders).
questions.zh-question:
一位年迈的女士以完全保有地产权(fee simple)的形式拥有一座大庄园。由于年事已高，她不愿再处理与房屋所有权相关的维护和其他义务。因此，她将庄园转让给她的长子，授予其终身地产权(life estate)，剩余权(remainder)授予她的小儿子。

三年后，小儿子病故，根据其合法订立的遗嘱，将其全部遗产留给了一位朋友。小儿子身后留有他的女儿，即其唯一继承人。六个月后，长子去世，在世的相关人有这位年迈的女士、那位朋友以及小儿子的女儿。

庄园所在地的司法管辖区承认关于或然剩余权(contingent remainders)可摧毁性的传统普通法规则。

在一场由这位年迈的女士、朋友和女儿之间为确定庄园所有权而提起的适当诉讼中，谁将胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 女儿，因为她是小儿子的继承人。
zh-choices.B: 年迈的女士，因为她拥有复归权(reversion)，该权利使其有权在长子去世后立即占有庄园。
zh-choices.C: 年迈的女士，因为小儿子的或然剩余权(contingent remainder)在他先于长子去世时被摧毁。
zh-choices.D: 朋友，因为小儿子的既定剩余权(vested remainder)已通过其遗嘱转让。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Future Interests
核心考点：既定剩余权 (Vested Remainder)

本题的关键在于识别小儿子的权益性质。当剩余权授予给一个已确定的人(ascertained person)且不受先决条件(condition precedent)限制时，它就是既定剩余权。

1. 产权转让 (Conveyance)
母亲 → 长子 (Life Estate)
母亲 → 小儿子 (Remainder)
分析： 小儿子是确定的，且获得产权没有额外条件（只要长子死，他一定得）。因此是 Vested Remainder。
2. 小儿子去世
小儿子立有遗嘱，将财产留给朋友。
法律后果： 既定剩余权是财产权益，可以通过遗嘱继承 (Devisable)。权益转移给朋友。
3. 长子去世
终身地产权 (Life Estate) 结束。
结果： 剩余权持有人（现在是朋友）获得占有权，成为 Fee Simple 所有者。
✅ 正确答案：D (朋友)

理由：

  • 小儿子拥有的是 Indefeasibly Vested Remainder（绝对既定剩余权）。
  • 这种权益在法律上等同于现有的财产权益，具有可转让性 (Alienable)、可遗赠性 (Devisable) 和 可继承性 (Descendible)。
  • 因为小儿子立了遗嘱，该权益根据遗嘱转移给了朋友，而不是通过无遗嘱继承法传给女儿。
⚠️ 常见陷阱 (Red Herring)

关于选项 C (Destructibility Rule)：

题目特意提到该管辖区承认“或然剩余权的可摧毁性规则” (Destructibility of Contingent Remainders)。这是一个干扰项。

该规则仅适用于或然剩余权 (Contingent Remainder)。例如：“给长子终身，如果小儿子那时年满21岁，则给小儿子”。

在本题中，小儿子的权益是既定的 (Vested)，因此该规则完全不适用。

为什么其他选项错误？

  • 选项 A (女儿)： 只有在小儿子没有遗嘱 (Intestate) 的情况下，女儿作为继承人才有份。但这里有有效遗嘱。
  • 选项 B (母亲)： 母亲已经把完整的 Fee Simple 拆分成了 Life Estate + Remainder 分别给了两个儿子，她自己没有保留任何权益 (No Reversion)。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord leased a building to a tenant for a 10-year term. Two years after the term began, the tenant subleased the building to a sublessee for a 5-year term. Under the terms of the sublease, the sublessee agreed to make monthly rent payments to the tenant.
Although the sublessee made timely rent payments to the tenant, the tenant did not forward four of those payments to the landlord. The tenant has left the jurisdiction and cannot be found. The landlord has sued the sublessee for the unpaid rent.
There is no applicable statute.
If the court rules that the sublessee is not liable to the landlord for the unpaid rent, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.A: A sublessee is responsible to the landlord only as a surety for unpaid rent owed by the tenant.
choices.B: The sublease constitutes a novation of the original lease.
choices.C: The sublessee is not in privity of estate or contract with the landlord.
choices.D: The sublessee's rent payments to the tenant fully discharged the sublessee's obligation to pay rent to the landlord.

questions.explanation:
Privity with landlord

Landlord
→
Tenant
→
Sublessee
→
Tenant
→
Landlord
Privity of contract & estate
No privity
Privity of contract & estate

A landlord and tenant have a legal relationship based on both:

  • privity of contract – their shared interest in the lease agreement and
  • privity of estate – their successive right to possess the property (ie, the tenant's current possessory right immediately precedes the landlord's future possessory right).

Either party can freely transfer his/her interest unless the lease prohibits it. For example, a tenant can sublease part of his/her interest to a third party (sublessee) for less than the remainder of the tenant's lease term. Despite that transfer, a sublessee is not liable to the landlord for a breach of the lease (eg, unpaid rent) because:

  • no lease agreement exists between the landlord and the sublessee (no privity of contract) and
  • the tenant will regain possession of the property before the landlord does (no privity of estate).

Instead, the tenant remains liable to the landlord for any such breach.

(Choice A) A surety is a person who assumes direct liability for another's obligation (eg, debt). Here, the sublessee is not a surety because there is no indication that the sublessee agreed to assume the tenant's contractual liability under the lease. Therefore, the sublessee is not liable for the tenant's failure to pay rent.

(Choice B) A novation is a separate agreement based on an existing contract that (1) substitutes a new party for an original contracting party and (2) excuses the original party from further performance under the original contract. But since a sublease does neither, it is not a novation.

(Choice D) A sublessee has no obligation to pay rent to a landlord.

📌 Educational Objective

Since a sublessee and landlord lack privity of contract and privity of estate, the sublessee is not liable to the landlord for a breach of the tenant's lease (eg, unpaid rent). Instead, the tenant remains liable to the landlord for any such breach.

📚 References
  • 49 Am. Jur. 2d Landlord and Tenant § 970 (2018).
questions.zh-question:
一位房东将一栋建筑物出租给一位承租人，租期为10年。租期开始两年后，承租人将该建筑物转租给一位次承租人，租期为5年。根据转租合同的条款，次承租人同意向承租人按月支付租金。

尽管次承租人及时向承租人支付了租金，但承租人并未将其中四笔租金转交给房东。承租人已离开该司法管辖区，下落不明。房东已就未付租金起诉次承租人。

本案没有适用的成文法。

如果法院裁定次承租人对房东的未付租金不承担责任，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 次承租人仅作为承租人所欠未付租金的保证人，向房东负责。
zh-choices.B: 该转租合同构成了对原租赁合同的更新(novation)。
zh-choices.C: 次承租人与房东之间不存在财产利益关系(privity of estate)或合同关系(privity of contract)。
zh-choices.D: 次承租人向承租人支付租金的行为，完全解除了次承租人向房东支付租金的义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Landlord & Tenant
核心考点：转租 (Sublease) vs. 转让 (Assignment) 在房产法中，承租人将租赁权转给第三方时，根据转让期限的不同，分为两种法律关系。这直接决定了第三方是否需要直接向房东负责。
法律关系图解
房东 (Landlord)
⬇️
承租人 (Tenant) (Privity of Contract & Estate)
⬇️ (转租 Sublease)
次承租人 (Sublessee)
❌ 房东与次承租人之间无直接连接
本案解析

要判断次承租人(Sublessee)是否对房东(Landlord)负责，必须看两者之间是否存在法律上的“关联”(Privity)。

1. 判定类型：是转租还是转让？

  • 转让 (Assignment)：承租人转让了剩余的全部租期。
  • 转租 (Sublease)：承租人只转让了部分租期，自己保留了未来的回归权 (Reversion)。

本案中，原租期剩8年（10年-2年），但只转给了次承租人 5年。承租人保留了最后3年的权益。因此，这是一个转租 (Sublease)。

2. 法律后果：

在转租关系中：

  • 无合同关系 (No Privity of Contract)：房东只和原承租人签了合同，没和次承租人签。
  • 无财产利益关系 (No Privity of Estate)：因为原承租人保留了部分权益（回归权），次承租人的占有权并不直接衔接房东的权益。
为什么选 C？
✅ 选项 C 正确

"The sublessee is not in privity of estate or contract with the landlord."

这是转租(Sublease)最核心的法律特征。因为缺乏这两种“Privity”中的任何一种，房东无法直接起诉次承租人要求支付租金。房东只能起诉原承租人(Tenant)，再由原承租人向次承租人追偿。

❌ 选项 A (Surety/保证人)

除非次承租人明确签署协议同意为原承租人的债务担保，否则法律不会自动将其视为保证人。

❌ 选项 B (Novation/债务更新)

Novation 需要三方（房东、承租人、次承租人）共同达成协议，明确房东同意释放原承租人的责任并由新人取代。单纯的转租不构成 Novation。

❌ 选项 D (Payment/支付行为)

次承租人向承租人付款是履行他们之间的转租合同，但这并不是免除对房东责任的法律理由。根本理由是次承租人对房东本来就没有直接责任。

💡 MBE 拿分技巧

看到 "Sublease vs. Assignment" 的题目，直接看剩余时间：

  • 转让全部剩余时间 ➡️ Assignment ➡️ 有 Privity of Estate ➡️ 要对房东负责。
  • 保留哪怕一天时间 ➡️ Sublease ➡️ 无 Privity ➡️ 不要对房东负责。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a tract of land in fee simple. Five years ago, he executed and delivered to his sister an instrument in the proper form of a warranty deed that conveyed the land to the sister "for and during the term of her natural life." No other estate or interest or person taking an interest was mentioned. The sister took possession of the land and has remained in possession.
Fifteen months ago, the man died, leaving a will that has been duly admitted to probate. The will, inter alia, had the following provision: "I devise the land to my wife for her natural life and from and after my wife's death to my son, his heirs and assigns, forever."
Administration of the man's estate has been completed. The man's wife claims the immediate right to possession of the land. His son also asserts a right to immediate possession.
In an appropriate lawsuit to which the sister, the wife, and the son are parties, who should be adjudged to have the right to immediate possession?

choices.A: The sister, because no subsequent act of the man would affect her life estate.
choices.B: The son, because the sister's estate terminated with the man's death and all that the man had was the right to transfer his reversion in fee simple.
choices.C: The wife, because the man's will was the final and definitive expression of his intent.
choices.D: The wife, because the sister's estate terminated with the death of the man.

questions.explanation:
Types of life estates
Words of purchase Words of limitation Defining characteristic
Life estate "To A" "for life" Ownership for duration of life of grantee
Life estate pur autre vie "To A" "for the life of B" Ownership for duration of life of person other than grantee

A life estate is a present possessory estate that terminates on the death of an individual. The future interest that follows a life estate is either a remainder (if created in a grantee) or a reversion (if retained by the grantor). If a grantor conveys a life estate without specifying who holds the future interest, then it is presumed that the grantor retains a reversion. This interest is fully transferable during the grantor's lifetime, devisable by will, and inheritable through intestate succession.

Here, the man conveyed a life estate in the land to his sister that would terminate when she died. The conveyance mentioned no other person or interest, so it is presumed that the man retained a reversion entitling him to possession of the land once the sister died. Until that time, however, the most the man could convey was his reversionary interest. Therefore, the man could do nothing that would affect the sister's life estate, and she should be adjudged to have the right to immediate possession of the land (Choices B, C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

If a grantor conveys a life estate without specifying who holds the future interest, the grantor presumptively retains a reversion.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 107 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing life estates).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子以完全所有权(fee simple)拥有一块土地。五年前，他签署并向其妹妹交付了一份格式正确的担保契据，将该土地转让给妹妹，“期限为她的自然生命期间”。契据中未提及任何其他产权、权益或享有权益的人。妹妹占有了该土地并持续占有至今。

十五个月前，该男子去世，留下了一份已正式通过遗嘱认证的遗嘱。该遗嘱除其他事项外，有如下条款：“我将此土地遗赠给我的妻子，期限为她的自然生命期间，并在我妻子去世后，永久遗赠给我的儿子及其继承人和受让人。”

该男子的遗产管理已经完成。该男子的妻子主张对该土地的即时占有权。他的儿子也主张即时占有权。

在一场以妹妹、妻子和儿子为当事人的适当诉讼中，谁应被判决拥有即时占有权？

zh-choices.A: 妹妹，因为该男子的任何后续行为都不会影响她的终身地产权。
zh-choices.B: 儿子，因为妹妹的地产权随着该男子的死亡而终止，而该男子所拥有的全部权利只是转让他以完全所有权(fee simple)享有的复归权。
zh-choices.C: 妻子，因为该男子的遗嘱是其意图的最终和明确的表达。
zh-choices.D: 妻子，因为妹妹的地产权随着该男子的死亡而终止。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：终身地产权与复归权

本题考察的是不动产法中关于终身地产权 (Life Estate) 的存续期间以及生前转让 (Inter Vivos Conveyance) 与遗嘱 (Will) 之间的效力层级。

核心法律概念

终身地产权 (Life Estate)：
一种赋予持有者在其有生之年占有和使用土地的权利。除非明确说明是“为他人之身” (pur autre vie)，否则其期限由持有者 (Grantee) 的寿命决定。

复归权 (Reversion)：
当原所有者 (Grantor) 转让出的权益少于其拥有的全部权益时（例如，拥有完全所有权却只转让了终身地产权），剩余的权益自动保留在原所有者手中。

逻辑推演步骤

第一步：分析五年前的转让行为
男子签署并交付了契据 (Deed)。这是一个有效的生前转让。
  • 受让人：妹妹。
  • 期限："for and during the term of her natural life"（在她自然生命期间）。
  • 结论：妹妹获得了以她自己的生命为量度的终身地产权。男子保留了复归权 (Reversion)。
权利状态时间轴
5年前：契据交付
妹妹获得现时占有权 (Possession)
↓
15个月前：男子去世
妹妹还活着 → 她的权利未终止
↓
现在：诉讼
妹妹仍享有占有权
第二步：分析男子去世的影响
男子的死亡不会终止妹妹的终身地产权。

因为契据中界定的期限是“妹妹的生命”，而不是“男子的生命”。只要妹妹还活着，她的地产权就继续存在。

第三步：分析遗嘱的效力
遗嘱 (Will) 只能处分死者在去世时实际拥有的财产。
  • 男子去世时，该土地的现时占有权属于妹妹。
  • 男子拥有的只是复归权 (Reversion)（即未来权益）。
  • 因此，遗嘱有效地将这个“复归权”传给了妻子（作为新的终身权益）和儿子（作为余留权人）。
  • 但是，妻子和儿子的权益必须等到妹妹去世后才能转变为占有权。
正确答案：A (妹妹)

妹妹拥有即时占有权，因为她的终身地产权尚未结束。男子的任何后续行为（包括立遗嘱）都不能单方面撤销已经有效交付的契据。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

选项 B (儿子)： 错误地认为妹妹的权益随男子死亡而终止。除非契据写明是“以男子的生命为期” (pur autre vie)，否则原所有者的死亡不影响受让人的终身地产权。
选项 C & D (妻子)： 错误。遗嘱不能推翻之前已经完成的生前转让。男子不能通过遗嘱把已经送给妹妹的“现时占有权”再送给妻子。他只能遗赠他剩下的东西（即等待妹妹去世后的复归权）。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
在做不动产题目时，牢记 "Nemo dat quod non habet"（人不能给付其本身未享有的权利）。

一旦题目中出现“契据已交付” (Deed delivered)，该权益就已经从授予人身上剥离了。授予人死后的遗嘱无法收回这部分权益。始终先画出时间轴，确定谁是“测量生命” (Measuring Life)。

reason.zh: 男子死亡时只能处分其仍拥有的归复权，而不能处分姐姐的占有性地产权。

reason.en: The question asks who may possess now, which is controlled by the surviving life estate.

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A retiree conveyed a condo he owned to "my son for life, remainder to my granddaughter." At the time of the conveyance, there was a mortgage on the condo with an unpaid balance of $25,000. The mortgage required monthly payments covering the interest to date and a portion of the principal.
For the past six months, the son has been living alone in the condo and paying the full monthly payment due to the lender. The son has since asked his lawyer for advice regarding the parties' obligations with respect to the monthly payment.
What should the lawyer tell him?

choices.A: The granddaughter and the son must pay based on the present value of their respective interests.
choices.B: The granddaughter must pay the full monthly payment.
choices.C: The son must pay the full monthly payment.
choices.D: The son must pay the principal, but the granddaughter must pay the interest to the lender.

questions.explanation:
Payment of preexisting mortgage obligation
Periodic payment of interest only
  • Life tenant is responsible for interest payments
  • Future-interest holder is responsible for principal payments due at later date
Periodic payment of interest & principal Life tenant & future-interest holder are responsible for payments equal to present value of each interest in property

A life estate is a present possessory interest in land that terminates on the death of an individual. It is typically followed by a reversion or a remainder. Payments on a mortgage incurred before the creation of the life estate are subject to allocation between the life tenant and the future-interest holder.

  • If the obligation is periodic payment of interest only, the life tenant pays interest and the future-interest holder pays principal.
  • If the obligation is periodic payment of both interest and the principal amount, it is allocated based on the present value of each interest.

Here, the retiree conveyed a life estate to his son and a remainder to his granddaughter. Since the mortgage requires monthly payments of both interest and principal, both the son and granddaughter are obligated to pay based on the present values of their interests. This explains why (Choices B, C & D) are incorrect.

📌 Educational Objective

If a preexisting mortgage obligation requires the periodic payment of interest only, then the life tenant pays the interest and the future-interest holder pays the later-due principal. But if periodic payment of interest and principal is required, then both payments must be allocated between the parties based on the present value of each interest.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 132 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing life tenant's obligation to contribute to a preexisting mortgage obligation when the principal amount has become due).
questions.zh-question:
主题：不动产法（Real Property）— 不动产所有权（Ownership of Real Property）

题目：
一名退休人员将其拥有的一套 condo 转让给“我的儿子终身享有（for life），余留给我的孙女（remainder to my granddaughter）”。在该转让发生时，这套 condo 上有一笔抵押贷款（mortgage），未偿余额为 25,000 美元。该 mortgage 要求每月付款，其中包括截至当期的利息以及部分本金。
过去六个月里，儿子一直独自居住在该 condo 中，并向贷款人（lender）支付到期的全部每月款项。此后，儿子就各方对每月付款义务的问题向律师咨询。
律师应当怎么告诉他？

zh-choices.A: 孙女和儿子必须按照各自权益的现值（present value）分担付款。
zh-choices.B: 孙女必须支付全部每月款项。
zh-choices.C: 儿子必须支付全部每月款项。
zh-choices.D: 儿子必须支付本金（principal），但孙女必须向贷款人支付利息（interest）。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A widow executed a will that devised a condominium unit to her only child, a son, for life and then to her named granddaughter "if she survives." The will named a charity as the alternate beneficiary of the condominium unit. The widow died and, 25 years later, the widow's son died. At the time of the son's death, the widow's granddaughter had been dead for three years. The granddaughter's will devised her entire estate to a friend.
In a dispute between the charity and the granddaughter's friend regarding ownership of the condominium unit, the court determined that the survivorship provision in the widow's will was ambiguous and awarded the condominium unit to the charity.
Which of the following is the most likely reason that the court awarded the condominium unit to the charity?

choices.A: The jurisdiction continues to follow the common law Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.B: The jurisdiction continues to follow the common law rule regarding the destructibility of contingent remainders.
choices.C: The jurisdiction has adopted the majority rule that the holder of a remainder interest must survive the owner of the immediately preceding estate.
choices.D: The jurisdiction's anti-lapse statute does not apply to the granddaughter.

questions.explanation:
Interpreting ambiguous survivorship conditions
transferor ↓
life tenant ↓
remainderman ↓
survivorship
condition ↓

Widow devised condominium “to my son for life, then to my granddaughter if she survives” the son.

Life estate
Contingent remainder
{ majority rule (survive preceding estate)
transferor ↓
life tenant ↓
remainderman ↓
survivorship
condition ↓

Widow devised condominium “to my son for life, then to my granddaughter if she survives” the widow.

Life estate
Contingent remainder
{ minority rule (survive transferor)

A remainder is a future interest that is capable of becoming possessory upon the natural expiration of a life estate or term of years (eg, “to my son for life, then to my granddaughter”). If a remainder is subject to a survivorship condition that is ambiguous as to whom the remainderman must survive (eg, “if she survives”), the condition will be construed as follows:

  • Majority rule – the remainderman must survive the owner of the immediately preceding estate (eg, the life tenant)
  • Minority rule – the remainderman must survive the transferor

Here, the granddaughter (remainderman) survived the widow (transferor) but not the son (life tenant). Since the court ruled that the charity was the owner of the condominium unit as the alternate beneficiary in the widow’s will, the jurisdiction must have adopted the majority rule. Otherwise, the granddaughter’s remainder interest would have vested upon the widow’s death and could have been devised by the granddaughter to her friend.

(Choice A) The Rule Against Perpetuities renders specific future interests void if they vest more than 21 years after lives in being. But the granddaughter’s interest did not violate this rule.

(Choice B) At common law, a contingent remainder was destroyed if the prior estate terminated before it vested. Since the granddaughter died before the son, this rule does not apply.

(Choice D) An anti-lapse statute prevents a devise from lapsing if certain devisees die before the testator. This is irrelevant here because the granddaughter survived the widow.

📌 Educational Objective

If a remainder is subject to an ambiguous survivorship condition (eg, “if she survives”), the majority rule is that the remainderman must survive the owner of the immediately preceding estate (eg, the life tenant) for the interest to become possessory. The minority rule is that the remainderman must survive the transferor.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Wills & Other Donative Transfers § 26.4 (Am. Law Inst. 2011) (construction of ambiguous survival condition).
