questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A brother and sister owned property as joint tenants. A two-family house was situated on the property. The brother lived in one of the two apartments and rented the other apartment to a friend. The brother got in a fight with the friend and injured him. The friend obtained and properly filed a judgment for $10,000 against the brother.
The statute in the jurisdiction reads: "Any judgment properly filed shall, for ten years from filing, be a lien on the real property then owned or subsequently acquired by any person against whom the judgment is rendered."
The sister, who lived in a distant city, knew nothing of the friend's judgment. Before the friend took any further action, the brother died. The common law joint tenancy is unmodified by statute. The sister then learned the facts and brought an appropriate action against the friend to quiet title to the property.
Does the friend have an enforceable judgment lien on the property?

choices.A: No, because the brother's death terminated the interest to which the friend's lien attached.
choices.B: No, because the sister had no actual notice of the friend's judgment until after the brother's death.
choices.C: Yes, because the friend was a tenant of both the brother and sister at the time of the judgment.
choices.D: Yes, but only against the brother's undivided one-half interest in the property, because the friend's judgment was filed prior to the brother's death.

questions.explanation:
Brother injures friend
Friend obtains judgment lien
Brother dies
(interest disappears)
Sister brings quiet title action
◀
▶
(judgment lien)
Sister's interest Brother's interest

A joint tenancy is a type of concurrent estate in which each tenant has an equal and undivided interest in the property with the right of survivorship. Under the common law (and in most jurisdictions), the creation and continuation of a joint tenancy depends on the coexistence of four unities (PITT):

  • Possession – tenants share an equal right to possess or use the property
  • Interest – tenants each have an equal interest in the property
  • Time – property interests simultaneously vest in all tenants
  • Title – property interests received in the same instrument of conveyance

A judgment lien on a joint tenant's interest does not disrupt the four unities because it merely secures payment of a money judgment (ie, the tenancy remains intact). But a forced sale of the encumbered property (eg, foreclosure) does sever the tenancy – and creates a tenancy in common – since the sale disrupts the unities of time and title. However, a joint tenant's property interest disappears upon his/her death and is absorbed by the surviving tenants due to the right of survivorship. Therefore, a judgment lien on the deceased tenant's property interest also disappears (as seen here).

(Choice B) The sister's notice of the friend's judgment has no bearing on the enforceability of his judgment lien on the brother's property interest.

(Choice C) Although the friend rented the apartment from the brother, he was a tenant of both siblings. But his judgment lien only encumbered the brother's property interest and disappeared upon the brother's death.

(Choice D) To create an enforceable judgment lien on a debtor's property, the judgment must be filed while the debtor owns that property. Therefore, the friend obtained an enforceable lien on the brother's one-half interest by filing the judgment before the brother's death. But the lien disappeared when the brother died.

📌 Educational Objective

Under a joint tenancy, a deceased tenant's property interest disappears and is absorbed by the surviving tenants due to the right of survivorship. As a result, a judgment lien on the deceased tenant's interest also disappears.
questions.zh-question:
一对兄妹以共同共有人的身份拥有一处房产。该房产上建有一栋双户住宅。哥哥住在其中一套公寓，并将另一套公寓出租给一位朋友。哥哥与该朋友发生争执并致其受伤。该朋友获得了针对哥哥的一项金额为10,000美元的判决，并进行了妥善登记。

该司法管辖区的法规规定：“任何妥善登记的判决，自登记之日起十年内，应成为对判决所针对的任何人当时拥有或随后获得的不动产的留置权。”

妹妹住在远方城市，对朋友的判决一无所知。在该朋友采取任何进一步行动之前，哥哥去世了。普通法上的共同共有关系未被法规修改。妹妹随后了解到事实，并对该朋友提起了适当的确认产权诉讼。

该朋友对该房产是否拥有可强制执行的判决留置权？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为哥哥的死亡终止了朋友留置权所附着的权益。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为直到哥哥去世后，妹妹才实际得知朋友的判决。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在判决作出时，该朋友是兄妹二人的租户。
zh-choices.D: 是，但仅针对哥哥在该房产中不可分割的二分之一权益，因为朋友的判决在哥哥去世前已经登记。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Joint Tenancy & Liens

✅ 正确答案：A

因为哥哥的死亡终止了朋友留置权所附着的权益。生存者权（Right of Survivorship）优于单纯的判决留置权（Judgment Lien）。

本题考察的是共同共有（Joint Tenancy）的核心特征以及判决留置权（Judgment Lien）对其的影响。

核心法则：生存者权 (Right of Survivorship)

在共同共有关系中，当一名共有人死亡时，其权益自动消失，并被尚存的共有人（Surviving Joint Tenants）吸收。尚存者并非从死者那里“继承”了权益，而是死者的权益单纯地终止了。

关键逻辑链条：

初始状态
哥哥 + 妹妹 = 共同共有 (Joint Tenants)
拥有完整的财产权益
↓
判决登记
朋友获得针对哥哥的判决留置权
留置权仅附着于哥哥的权益上
↓
关键事件：哥哥死亡
哥哥的权益瞬间消失 (Extinguished)
妹妹通过生存者权拥有全部
↓
最终结果
皮之不存，毛将焉附？
哥哥权益消失 → 留置权随之消失
妹妹拥有无负担的房产

为什么留置权没有“分割”共有关系？

这是MBE的一个常见陷阱。

1. 单纯的留置权不分割（Lien does not sever）： 仅仅登记判决（Filing a judgment）通常不足以破坏共同共有的“四个统一体”（Four Unities）。它只是在债务人的权益上设立了一个担保。

2. 需要强制执行（Execution/Levy）： 如果朋友在哥哥生前不仅仅是登记了判决，而是启动了强制执行程序（Levy and Sale），那么这种强制出售行为会分割共有关系，将其转变为按份共有（Tenancy in Common）。

3. 赌博性质： 债权人（朋友）实际上是在与死神赛跑。如果债务人（哥哥）先死，留置权消失；如果债务人先被强制执行，留置权得以实现。本案中，哥哥先死，所以朋友输了。

选项 B 错误 通知（Notice）无关紧要： 妹妹是否知情不影响生存者权的法律效力。
选项 D 错误 最具迷惑性： 很多人认为留置权会“锁定”哥哥的一半权益。但如上所述，除非已经执行（Levy），否则哥哥死后其权益归零，留置权无处附着。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)
看到 Joint Tenancy + Lien/Mortgage + Death 的组合时：
  • 如果是抵押 (Mortgage)：在“产权理论州 (Title Theory)”可能导致分割；在“留置权理论州 (Lien Theory)”不分割。MBE通常默认 Lien Theory。
  • 如果是判决留置权 (Judgment Lien)：仅仅登记（Filing）绝不导致分割。
  • 结论： 如果没有发生强制出售，债务人死亡 = 留置权/抵押权（在Lien Theory下）消灭。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
The owner of an apartment building leased an apartment to a tenant at a fixed monthly rent for one year. Seven months later, the tenant informed the owner of her intent to vacate the premises. The tenant vacated the premises and did not pay rent for the remaining five months of the lease. The owner did not enter the premises during those five months, and he made no effort to rent the unoccupied space to someone else. Subsequently, the owner sued the tenant for the five months of unpaid rent.
According to the majority rule, is the owner entitled to recover the full amount of this unpaid rent from the tenant?

choices.A: No, because the owner accepted the tenant's surrender of her leasehold interest.
choices.B: No, because the owner made no effort to rent the apartment to someone else.
choices.C: Yes, because the owner did not retake possession of the leased premises.
choices.D: Yes, because the tenant abandoned her leasehold interest.

questions.explanation:
Unjustifiable abandonment of leased property

Offer to surrender rights
  • Tenant abandoned leased property
  • with intent to terminate lease without legal justification (eg, by refusing to pay rent)
Offer accepted
  • By landlord's express agreement
  • By landlord retaking possession of property plus either:
    • landlord's own use of property
    • re-renting property to third party
▼
Lease terminated
Tenant not liable for future rent
Offer rejected
▼
Lease continues
Tenant liable for future rent
▼
Duty to mitigate damages
  • Majority rule: landlord must make reasonable effort to re-rent property
  • Minority rule: no duty to mitigate

A tenant's unjustifiable abandonment of leased property is treated as an offer to surrender the tenant's rights under the lease. The landlord may accept that offer or reject it. A landlord who rejects the offer may continue to enforce the lease, and the tenant remains liable for rent. But under the majority rule, the landlord must mitigate damages by making a reasonable effort to re-rent the premises to recover the full amount of unpaid rent.

Here, the tenant abandoned the apartment seven months into the lease by vacating the premises and refusing to pay rent. There are no facts indicating that the abandonment was justified or that the owner accepted the tenant's offer (Choices A & D). However, the owner made no effort to re-rent the apartment to mitigate damages as required by the majority rule. Therefore, the owner is not entitled to recover the full amount of the unpaid rent from the tenant.

(Choice C) A landlord's retaking of the abandoned premises, coupled with re-renting or personally using the premises, may be treated as an acceptance of an offer to surrender. Here, though the owner did not retake possession of the premises, he is not entitled to unpaid rent because he failed to mitigate damages.

📌 Educational Objective

If a landlord rejects a tenant's unjustifiable abandonment of leased property, the landlord may continue to enforce the lease and the tenant must continue to pay rent. But under the majority rule, to recover the full amount of unpaid rent, the landlord must mitigate damages by making a reasonable effort to re-rent the property.

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A pastor owned a vacant one-acre tract of land. Five years ago, he executed a deed conveying the land to "my church for the purpose of erecting a church building thereon." Three years ago, the pastor died, leaving his son as his sole heir at law. His duly probated will left "all my Estate, both real and personal, to my friend."
The church never constructed a church building on the land, and last month the church, for a valid consideration, conveyed the land to a real estate developer.
The real estate developer brought an appropriate action to quiet title against the son, the friend, and the church, and joined the appropriate state official. Such official asserted that a charitable trust was created that has not terminated.
In such action, who should the court find for?

choices.A: The friend.
choices.B: The real estate developer.
choices.C: The son.
choices.D: The state official.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible
Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible, Durational
Fee simple determinable
  • “so long as”
  • “during”
  • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest (ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Defeasible, Conditional
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • “but if”
  • “provided that”
  • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

Like fee simple absolutes (FSAs) and other freehold estates,† defeasible fees are ownership interests in land that last for an indeterminate duration. But unlike FSAs, defeasible fees may be terminated by the happening of a stated event. Defeasible fees are limited by specific durational or conditional language (eg, “so long as,” “but if”). However, language that limits only the purpose of the transfer (eg, “for the purpose of”) creates an FSA.

Here, the pastor conveyed the land “to my church for the purpose of erecting a church building thereon.” This conveyance created an FSA — not a defeasible fee — so the fact that the church never constructed a church building on the land did not terminate its ownership interest in the land. Therefore, the church effectively conveyed the land to the real estate developer, and the real estate developer should win the action.

†To be categorized as a freehold (eg, life estates, estates in fee), an estate must be immobile (eg, land, fixtures) AND last for an indeterminate duration (eg, for the life of X). In contrast, a leasehold is an immobile estate that lasts for a limited duration (eg, 15 years).

(Choices A & C) Had the church’s ownership interest in the land terminated and reverted back to the pastor, the friend — not the son — would own the land because the pastor’s will left his entire estate to the friend.

(Choice D) A trust is an arrangement in which a trustee holds property at the request of another (settlor) for the benefit of a third party (beneficiary). A charitable trust is one created for a charitable purpose, and it is enforceable by the appropriate state official (ie, the attorney general). But here, no trust was created since the church is the beneficiary and the holder of the property (no trustee).

📌 Educational Objective

Defeasible fees are limited by specific durational or conditional language. Language that limits only the purpose of the transfer instead creates a fee simple absolute.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 44 cmt. m (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing designated purpose of conveyance).
questions.zh-question:
一位牧师拥有一块一英亩的空地。五年前，他签署了一份地契，将该土地转让给“我的教会，用于在其上建造一座教堂建筑”。三年前，牧师去世，其儿子是其唯一法定继承人。他经过适当遗嘱认证的遗嘱将“我所有的动产和不动产”留给了“我的朋友”。

该教会从未在该土地上建造教堂建筑，上个月，该教会以有效的对价将该土地转让给了一位房地产开发商。

该房地产开发商对该儿子、朋友和教会提起了适当的确认产权诉讼(action to quiet title)，并将相应的州政府官员列为当事人。该官员主张，一项慈善信托已经设立且尚未终止。

在此诉讼中，法院应判决谁胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 朋友。
zh-choices.B: 房地产开发商。
zh-choices.C: 儿子。
zh-choices.D: 州政府官员。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Estates in Land
核心考点：转让目的 vs. 限制条件 在不动产转让中，仅仅陈述土地使用的目的（Purpose）或动机（Motive），并不会创设可作废的保有权（Defeasible Fee）。相反，这通常被视为创设了绝对完全保有地产权（Fee Simple Absolute）。

案情逻辑分析

本题的关键在于解读地契中的措辞：

"to my church for the purpose of erecting a church building thereon"

（给我的教会，用于在其上建造一座教堂建筑）

1. 法律定性：
这句话使用了 "for the purpose of"（为了...目的）。在普通法中，这种表达被视为祈使性语言（Precatory Language），它表达了授予人的愿望，但没有施加法律上的强制力或终止条件。

2. 结果：
因为没有使用创设“可作废保有权”所需的特定词汇（如 "so long as", "but if"），教会获得的是绝对完全保有地产权 (Fee Simple Absolute)。

3. 结论：
既然是绝对完全保有权，教会拥有土地的全部权益。即使教会没有建教堂，土地也不会自动复归给牧师的继承人。因此，教会将土地卖给开发商是完全有效的。

类型 关键措辞 (Magic Words) 法律后果
绝对完全保有权
Fee Simple Absolute		 "To A"
"For the purpose of..."
"With the hope that..."		 拥有完整所有权，不受条件限制。
可决定终止的保有权
Fee Simple Determinable		 "So long as"
"While"
"During"		 条件触发时，自动复归 (Automatic Reverter)。
受后决条件限制的保有权
Fee Simple Subject to Condition Subsequent		 "But if"
"Provided that"
"On condition that"		 条件触发时，需行使进入权 (Right of Entry)。

为什么选 B (房地产开发商)？

正确。 因为教会获得了 Fee Simple Absolute，其所有权不因未建教堂而终止。教会拥有合法的处分权，将其卖给了开发商。开发商现在拥有该土地的有效产权。

为什么其他选项错误？

A (朋友) & C (儿子)：
这两个选项都基于一个错误的前提：即教会失去了土地所有权。

如果地契创造的是 Defeasible Fee 且条件已触发，土地会复归给牧师的遗产。由于牧师遗嘱将所有财产留给了朋友，朋友会优于法定继承人（儿子）获得土地。但因为本案中土地从未复归，所以两人都无权。

D (州政府官员)：
州官员主张存在慈善信托 (Charitable Trust)。虽然信托可以由州检察长（Attorney General）强制执行，但本案中并没有设立信托的意图。

仅仅将财产赠予慈善机构（教会）并说明用途，通常被视为绝对赠与 (Outright Gift)，而不是设立信托。除非有明确证据表明授予人意图让教会作为受托人（Trustee）持有财产，否则不构成信托。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在 Real Property 题目中，法院倾向于促进土地的自由流转 (Free Alienation of Land)。

因此，如果地契语言模棱两可（例如只是表达目的、愿望），法院几乎总是将其解释为 Fee Simple Absolute，而不是可能会导致土地所有权丧失的 Defeasible Fee。

口诀：没有 "So long as" 或 "But if"，通常就不是条件！

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An elderly woman had two children, a son and daughter. In the months before the woman's death, the son had lived in the woman's home and cared for her. Although the daughter had provided no assistance to the woman, both children inherited the woman's home upon her death and became tenants in common.
The son continued to live in the woman's home and paid all taxes, insurance, and other carrying charges on the property. The daughter never visited the property and did not seek rent or other compensation from the son until they got into a heated dispute 15 years later.
The son has filed an action to quiet title and claims that he owns the property in fee simple. The period of time to acquire title by adverse possession in the jurisdiction is 10 years.
Who is likely to prevail?

choices.A: The daughter, because one co-tenant cannot acquire title by adverse possession against another.
choices.B: The daughter, because there is no evidence that the son has ousted the daughter.
choices.C: The son, because he has acquired title in fee simple by adverse possession.
choices.D: The son, because the parties' acts indicate the daughter's intention to renounce her inheritance.

questions.explanation:
Ways of ousting a co-tenant

Adverse possession allows a person to acquire title to another's property when his/her possession of the land is:

  • Open and notorious — apparent or visible to a reasonable owner
  • Continuous — uninterrupted for the statutory period
  • Exclusive — not shared with the owner
  • Actual — physical presence on the land
  • Nonpermissive — hostile and adverse to the owner

But for a co-tenant to acquire sole ownership of co-owned property through adverse possession, he/she must also oust the other co-tenants. This is done by preventing them from using or accessing the property (eg, changing the locks, constructing a fence, physical removal) (Choice A).

Here, the son (co-tenant) lived alone on the property and paid all taxes, insurance, and other carrying charges for more than the 10-year statutory period. But since he took no action to prevent the daughter (other co-tenant) from using the property, he did not oust her. Therefore, he never acquired sole ownership by adverse possession, and the daughter will likely prevail (Choice C).

(Choice D) An inheritance can only be renounced if the recipient unequivocally rejects the inheritance within a reasonable time after learning of it. Actions that merely indicate an intent to renounce are not sufficient. Therefore, the parties' actions—absent an explicit rejection—did not eliminate the daughter's right to the inherited property.

📌 Educational Objective

A co-tenant can acquire sole ownership of co-owned property through adverse possession if he/she ousts the other co-tenants by preventing them from using or accessing the property (and meets all other requirements for adverse possession).
questions.zh-question:
一位年迈的妇人有两个孩子，一个儿子和一个女儿。在该妇人去世前的几个月里，儿子一直住在她的家里并照顾她。尽管女儿没有向妇人提供任何帮助，但在她去世后，两个孩子都继承了她的房屋，并成为共同共有人 (tenants in common)。

儿子继续住在这所房子里，并支付了该房产的所有税款、保险费和其他持有费用。女儿从未探访过该房产，也未向儿子索要租金或其他补偿，直到15年后他们发生激烈争执。

儿子提起了确认产权诉讼 (action to quiet title)，并声称他拥有该房产的完全所有权 (fee simple)。在该司法管辖区，通过侵权逆占 (adverse possession) 取得所有权的法定时效为10年。

谁可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 女儿，因为一个共同共有人不能通过侵权逆占来对抗另一个共同共有人从而获得所有权。
zh-choices.B: 女儿，因为没有证据表明儿子已经驱逐 (ousted) 了女儿。
zh-choices.C: 儿子，因为他已经通过侵权逆占取得了完全所有权 (fee simple)。
zh-choices.D: 儿子，因为双方的行为表明女儿意图放弃其继承权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Adverse Possession
核心法律规则：驱逐 (Ouster)

在共同共有 (Tenancy in Common) 关系中，一个共有人要通过侵权逆占 (Adverse Possession) 取得另一个共有人的产权，仅有“独占使用”是不够的，必须发生明确的驱逐 (Ouster)。

📝 案情逻辑推演

1. 默认规则：占有即共享
法律假定，任何一个共同共有人 (Co-tenant) 对房产的占有，都是代表所有共有人进行的。因此，儿子的居住通常被视为也代表了女儿的权益。这种占有在法律上不具有敌意 (Not Hostile)。
2. 仅仅支付费用 ≠ 敌意占有
儿子支付税款、保险费等 (Carrying charges)，被视为他在行使作为共有人的管理职责，或者作为他独占使用房产的对价，但这并不构成对女儿产权的否认。
3. 关键缺失：驱逐 (Ouster)
要启动侵权逆占的时效，儿子必须采取行动阻止女儿进入或使用房产（例如换锁并拒绝给钥匙、明确告知“这是我的房子，你滚出去”）。

结论 题目中明确指出儿子没有阻止女儿使用房产，因此没有发生 Ouster，10年的时效从未开始计算。

🔍 选项深度解析

选项 分析
A
法律错误 		错误观点：共有人之间永远不能逆占。
修正：共有人可以逆占，但门槛很高，必须证明发生了 Ouster。
B
正确答案 		正确理由：直接击中考点。没有证据表明儿子驱逐了女儿 (No Ouster)，因此逆占要素中的“敌意 (Hostile)”不成立。
C
事实错误 		虽然时间超过10年，但由于缺乏敌意占有的起始点 (Ouster)，儿子并未获得 Fee Simple。
D
概念混淆 		放弃继承 (Renunciation) 需要明确的书面行为或法庭程序。仅仅是不访问、不收租金，在法律上不构成放弃产权。
💡 MBE 避坑指南 在处理 Co-tenants 之间的 Adverse Possession 问题时：
  • 看到 "Sole possession" (独自居住) → 不够。
  • 看到 "Paying all taxes" (支付所有税费) → 不够。
  • 必须寻找 "Prevented entry" (阻止进入) 或 "Refused access" (拒绝访问) 等明确表示 Ouster 的行为。

reason.zh: 触发共有人之间逆占需具备驱逐规则的适用。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A manicurist entered into a one-year agreement to lease a nail salon from a landlord. During the first six months of the lease, the plumbing in the building functioned properly. During the seventh month, a pipe under the bathroom sink began leaking over a three-day weekend, causing flooding throughout the nail salon. The manicurist took reasonable steps to mitigate damages, including turning off the water to the bathroom sink and cleaning up the excess water to prevent water damage to the floors. The manicurist was still able to operate the nail salon despite the leaking pipe but not at full capacity. She notified the landlord about the leaking pipe, but the landlord refused to repair the faulty plumbing. The manicurist refused to pay the following month's rent, and the landlord has filed a breach-of-contract action against her.
For whom is the court likely to decide?

choices.A: For the landlord, because he did not have a duty to repair the plumbing.
choices.B: For the landlord, because the implied covenant of quiet enjoyment does not apply to commercial leases.
choices.C: For the manicurist, because she took reasonable steps to mitigate damages.
choices.D: For the manicurist, because the leaking pipe resulted in a constructive eviction.

questions.explanation:
Landlord's duty to repair leased premises
Type of lease Common law Majority rule
Residential No duty to repair unless statute or contract requires Duty to repair substantial defects under implied warranty of habitability
Commercial No duty to make ordinary repairs unless statute or contract requires

Although most jurisdictions today impose an implied warranty of habitability on residential leases, courts are reluctant to impose the implied warranty of habitability on commercial leases. As a result, a landlord of leased commercial property generally has no duty to make repairs unless:

  • the repair is so substantial that it would not ordinarily fall within the tenant's common-law duty to repair or
  • the repair would primarily benefit the value of the landlord's property.

Examples of repairs that might fall on the landlord include major structural damage (eg, to the roof or foundation).

Here, the manicurist leased a nail salon (ie, commercial property) from the landlord. The leaking pipe under the bathroom sink was an ordinary repair that did not amount to major structural damage and did not primarily benefit the value of the landlord's property. Therefore, the landlord had no duty to repair the plumbing. Because the manicurist refused to pay rent even though the landlord had no such duty, the landlord will likely prevail in this breach-of-contract action.

(Choice B) The implied covenant of quiet enjoyment applies to both residential and commercial leases. It is a promise by the landlord not to interfere with the tenant's possession of the leased premises. Here, the landlord's refusal to repair the plumbing did not interfere with the manicurist's possession since she continued to operate the nail salon.

(Choice C) Although an injured party generally has a duty to mitigate damages, that duty is irrelevant here. The manicurist's duty to mitigate damages does not create a landlord's duty to repair or justify the manicurist's refusal to pay rent.

(Choice D) Constructive eviction occurs when a landlord's wrongful act or omission substantially interferes with the tenant's use and enjoyment of the leased premises, causing the tenant to vacate within a reasonable time. Here, the landlord had no duty to repair the plumbing. Moreover, the manicurist continued to operate the nail salon despite the leak, so she was not constructively evicted.

📌 Educational Objective

A commercial landlord generally has no duty to make ordinary repairs unless required by statute or contract. A commercial landlord may have a duty to repair only if (1) the repair is so substantial that it would not ordinarily fall within the tenant's common-law duty to repair or (2) the repair would primarily benefit the value of the landlord's property.

📚 References
  • 49 Am. Jur. 2d Landlord & Tenant § 443 (2020) (stating that the implied warranty of habitability does not apply to commercial leases).

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned adjoining lots (Lot 1 and Lot 2) in fee simple. He built a house in which he took up residence on Lot 1. Thereafter, he built a house on Lot 2, which he sold, house and lot, to his brother. Consistent with the contract of sale and purchase, a valid deed conveying Lot 2 from the man to the brother contained the following clause:
"In the event my brother, his heirs or assigns, decide to sell the property hereby conveyed and obtain a purchaser ready, willing, and able to purchase Lot 2 and the improvements thereon on terms and conditions acceptable to my brother, said Lot 2 and improvements shall be offered to me, my heirs or assigns, on the same terms and conditions. I, my heirs or assigns, as the case may be, shall have ten days from said offer to accept said offer and thereby to exercise said option."
Three years after delivery and recording of the deed and payment of the purchase price, the brother became ill and moved to a climate more compatible with his health. The brother's daughter orally offered to purchase the premises from him at its then fair market value. The brother declined his daughter's offer but instead deeded Lot 2 to his daughter as a gift.
Immediately thereafter, the daughter sold Lot 2 to her friend at the then fair market value of Lot 2. The sale was completed by the delivery of deed and payment of the purchase price. At no time did the brother or his daughter offer to sell Lot 2 to the man.
The man learned of the conveyance to the daughter and the sale to the friend one week after the conveyance of Lot 2 from the daughter to the friend. The man promptly brought an appropriate action against the friend to enforce rights created in him by the deed of the man to the brother. The man tendered the amount paid by the friend into the court for whatever disposition the court deemed proper.
The common-law Rule Against Perpetuities is unmodified by statute.
Which of the following will determine whether the man will prevail?

choices.A: The parol evidence rule only.
choices.B: The parol evidence rule and the Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.C: The Rule Against Perpetuities only.
choices.D: The statute of frauds and the type of recording statute of the jurisdiction in question.

questions.explanation:
Rule against perpetuities (RAP)
Does grantee have a contingent future interest?
  • Contingent remainder
  • Vested remainder subject to open
  • Executory interest
  • Power of appointment
  • Right of first refusal
  • Option
No
RAP does not apply
Yes
RAP applies
Must vesting event occur within 21 years after creation of interest?
Yes
Interest valid
No
Could interest possibly vest >21 years after validating life ends?
No
Interest valid
Yes
Common law = interest void
Majority rule = wait & see for 90 years

The Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) applies only to contingent future interests—ie, future interests that are held by unknown/unborn persons or subject to a condition precedent. A right of first refusal is a contractual right to purchase property before any other person if the owner later decides to sell, so it must comply with RAP.

Under the common-law RAP, a contingent future interest is void ab initio (ie, from the beginning) if there is any possibility that it could vest more than 21 years after some relevant life in being at the creation of the interest. Therefore, a right of first refusal almost always violates RAP if the conveying instrument does not provide a termination date† that falls within the perpetuities period.

Here, there is no termination date for the man's right of first refusal. As a result, it is possible that the right of first refusal may not vest until after the perpetuities period—ie, more than 21 years after the man and brother have died. Since this RAP violation renders the man's right of first refusal invalid, RAP determines whether he will prevail in this action.

†A termination date can be set by a temporal limitation (eg, calendar date) or by reference to a life in being (eg, within 21 years of grantee's death).

(Choices A & B) The parol evidence rule generally bars evidence of a prior agreement to modify or contradict the terms of a final written agreement. But here, the man is seeking to enforce not a prior agreement but the purchase option specified in the deed.

(Choice D) The statute of frauds renders certain contracts, including contracts for the sale of land, unenforceable unless they are in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. Additionally, recording statutes protect earlier-recorded property interests against subsequent purchasers. But neither will protect the man's contingent future interest from being invalidated by RAP.

📌 Educational Objective

The Rule Against Perpetuities applies to contingent future interests, including a right of first refusal. This contractual right violates RAP if it is not set to terminate within 21 years after some relevant life in being at the creation of the interest.

📚 References
  • 61 Am. Jur. 2d Perpetuities and Restraints on Alienation § 5 (2020) (Rule Against Perpetuities).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子以完全所有权（fee simple）拥有相邻地块（地块1和地块2）。他在地块1上建造了一座房屋并居住于此。此后，他在地块2上建造了一座房屋，并将房屋和地块一同出售给了他的兄弟。根据买卖合同，一份将地块2从该男子转让给其兄弟的有效契约包含以下条款：

“若我的兄弟、其继承人或受让人决定出售本协议转让的财产，并找到一位准备好、愿意且有能力按我兄弟可接受的条款和条件购买地块2及其上附着物的买家，则上述地块2及其附着物应以相同的条款和条件向我、我的继承人或受让人发出要约（offer）。我、我的继承人或受让人（视情况而定）应在收到上述要约之日起十天内接受该要约，从而行使该选择权。”

在契约交付、登记并支付购买价款三年后，该兄弟生病并搬到一个气候更适合其健康的地方。该兄弟的女儿口头要约（offer）以当时的市场公允价值向他购买该房产。该兄弟拒绝了他女儿的要约，而是将地块2作为赠与过户给了他的女儿。

此后，该女儿立即以当时地块2的市场公允价值将其出售给了她的朋友。此次出售通过交付契约和支付购买价款完成。该兄弟或其女儿从未向该男子要约出售地块2。

在该女儿将地块2转让给朋友一周后，该男子得知了此次转让和出售事宜。该男子立即对该朋友提起了适当的诉讼，以强制执行由他与兄弟之间的契约赋予他的权利。该男子将朋友支付的款项提存至法院，以供法院做出其认为适当的处置。

普通法上的 Rule Against Perpetuities 未被成文法修改。

以下哪项将决定该男子是否会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 仅限口头证据规则。
zh-choices.B: 口头证据规则和 Rule Against Perpetuities。
zh-choices.C: 仅限 Rule Against Perpetuities。
zh-choices.D: 防止欺诈法和该司法管辖区的登记法规类型。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property (不动产法)

🎯 核心考点：Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP)

本题考察的是反永久占有规则（RAP）对优先购买权（Right of First Refusal）的适用性。

1. 识别权利类型

题目中的条款赋予了卖方（Man）一项权利：如果买方（Brother）决定出售土地，必须先向卖方要约。这在法律上被称为 Right of First Refusal（优先购买权）。

2. 法律规则适用

在普通法下，优先购买权被视为一种附条件的未来权益（Contingent Future Interest）。因此，它必须遵守 Rule Against Perpetuities。

  • RAP 规则：权益必须在“设立时的在世之人的寿命 + 21年”内归属（vest）或失效。
  • 违规后果：如果存在任何可能性（哪怕是理论上的），该权益在上述期限后才归属，则该权益自始无效（Void ab initio）。
3. 结合本案事实

请注意契约中的措辞：

"...In the event my brother, his heirs or assigns... said Lot 2... shall be offered to me, my heirs or assigns..."

这里使用了“继承人或受让人”（heirs or assigns），且没有设定时间限制。

这意味着：

  • 该权利可能在几百年后，当双方的曾曾孙子决定出售土地时才被触发。
  • 这显然超过了“在世人寿命 + 21年”的期限。
⚖️ 结论：
该优先购买权违反了 RAP，因此自始无效。
决定胜诉与否的关键是 RAP。
正确答案：C
为何其他选项错误？

❌ A & B (Parol Evidence Rule): 口头证据规则用于排除与书面合同矛盾的先前口头协议。本案中，男子依据的是契约（Deed）中的书面条款，而非口头协议，因此该规则不适用。

❌ D (Statute of Frauds/Recording):
  • 防止欺诈法要求土地合同必须书面（本案已有书面契约）。
  • 登记法规涉及对抗第三人（本案契约已登记）。
虽然这些都很重要，但它们无法挽救一个因违反 RAP 而本质上无效的条款。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在 MBE 不动产题目中，如果你看到：

  1. 购买选择权 (Option to Purchase) 或 优先购买权 (Right of First Refusal)；
  2. 且条款中包含 "heirs and assigns"（及于继承人和受让人）；
  3. 且没有明确的截止日期（如“21年内”）；

请立即联想 RAP。这通常是导致该权利无效的原因。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A husband owned a farm of 300 acres in fee simple. He died and by will duly admitted to probate devised the farm to his surviving widow for life with remainder in fee simple to his three children (twin sons and a daughter). All three children survived the husband.
At the time of the husband's death, there existed a mortgage on the farm that the husband had given 10 years before to secure a loan for the purchase of the farm. At his death, there remained unpaid $40,000 in principal, payable in installments of $4,000 per year for the next 10 years. In addition, there was due interest at the rate of 10% per annum, payable annually with the installment of principal. The widow took possession and out of a gross income of $50,000 per year realized $25,000 net after paying all expenses and charges except the installment of principal and interest due on the mortgage.
The twin sons wanted the three children, including the daughter, to each contribute one-third of the amounts needed to pay the mortgage installments. The daughter objected, contending that the widow should pay all of these amounts out of the profits she had made in operation of the farm. When foreclosure of the mortgage seemed imminent, the daughter sought legal advice.
If the daughter obtained sound advice relating to her rights, what was she told?

choices.A: Her only protection would lie in instituting an action for partition to compel the sale of the life estate of the widow and to obtain the value of the daughter's one-third interest in remainder.
choices.B: She could be compelled personally to pay her share of the amounts due because discharge of the mortgage enhances the principal.
choices.C: She could not be held personally liable for any amount but her share in remainder could be lost if the mortgage installments are not paid.
choices.D: She could obtain appropriate relief to compel the widow personally to pay the sums due because the income is more than adequate to cover these amounts.

questions.explanation:
Life tenant's duties
Duty to pay current charges Life tenant must pay all current charges due during life tenancy (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest) up to financial benefit received from property
Duty to prevent waste Life tenant must prevent affirmative waste (ie, voluntary waste), permissive waste & ameliorative waste
Duty to make ordinary repairs Life tenant must make reasonable repairs to preserve property

The holder of a life estate (ie, the life tenant) has a duty to pay interest on any encumbrances on the land (eg, mortgages) that becomes due during the life tenancy. However, this duty is limited to the amount of income generated by the property or, if none, to the extent of the reasonable rental value of the property. And any future-interest holders (ie, reversioners or remaindermen) must pay the principal to protect their interests.

Here, the husband devised a life estate in the farm to his widow and a remainder to his three children. The farm's income is more than adequate to cover the mortgage interest, so the widow (life tenant) must pay the interest due on the mortgage. But the children (remaindermen) must pay the principal installments (Choice D). Therefore, the daughter must contribute her one-third share of the principal installments or risk losing her remainder interest.

(Choice A) Partition is a remedy available to owners of concurrent interests in property (eg, tenants in common) - not to owners of successive interests in property (eg, life tenants and remaindermen).

(Choice B) The daughter cannot be compelled to pay her share of the principal installments, but she could lose her remainder interest if she fails to do so.

📌 Educational Objective

The holder of a life estate (ie, life tenant) has a duty to pay interest on any encumbrances on the property, but the future-interest holder (ie, reversioner or remainderman) must pay the principal.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property §§ 129 - 30 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (life tenant's duty to pay taxes and other charges).
questions.zh-question:
一位丈夫以完全保有地产权(fee simple)的形式拥有一个占地300英亩的农场。他去世后，其经正式遗嘱检验程序承认的遗嘱将该农场遗赠给其在世的遗孀终身保有(for life)，剩余的完全保有地产权(remainder in fee simple)则归其三个子女（一对双胞胎儿子和一个女儿）所有。三个子女均在丈夫去世时在世。

在丈夫去世时，该农场上存在一笔按揭贷款，是丈夫在十年前为购买该农场而设定的担保贷款。在他去世时，尚有4万美元本金未偿还，需在未来十年内以每年4000美元的分期付款方式支付。此外，尚有年利率10%的到期利息，需与本金分期款一同按年支付。遗孀占有了该农场，在每年5万美元的总收入中，扣除除按揭贷款的本金和利息分期款之外的所有开支和费用后，获得了2.5万美元的净收入。

这对双胞胎儿子希望包括女儿在内的三个子女每人承担支付按揭分期款所需金额的三分之一。女儿表示反对，主张遗孀应从其经营农场所得的利润中支付所有这些款项。当按揭止赎似乎迫在眉睫时，女儿寻求了法律咨询。

如果女儿获得了关于其权利的合理建议，她会被告知什么？

zh-choices.A: 她唯一的保护措施在于提起分割诉讼，以强制出售遗孀的终身地产权，并获得女儿所拥有的三分之一剩余权益的价值。
zh-choices.B: 她可能被强制个人支付她应付的份额，因为清偿按揭贷款增加了本金的价值。
zh-choices.C: 她个人无需对任何金额承担责任，但如果按揭分期款未被支付，她所拥有的剩余权益份额可能会丧失。
zh-choices.D: 她可以获得适当的救济，以强制遗孀个人支付到期款项，因为农场收入足以支付这些款项。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Life Estates & Mortgages
核心考点：按揭贷款的分摊规则 在不动产法中，当财产被分割为终身地产权 (Life Estate) 和剩余权 (Remainder) 时，财产上的按揭贷款 (Mortgage) 支付责任有明确的划分：

角色 支付责任 逻辑依据
终身地产权人
(Life Tenant)		 支付利息 (Interest) 享受当前的收益和占有权，应承担当前的资金成本。
剩余权人
(Remainderman)		 支付本金 (Principal) 本金偿还增加了财产的净值，这部分利益最终归属于未来获得财产的人。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 C)

法律依据：根据普通法规则，终身地产权人（本案中的遗孀）有义务支付按揭贷款的利息，但仅限于其从土地获得的收入或土地的合理租金价值。而剩余权人（本案中的女儿和双胞胎儿子）负责支付按揭贷款的本金。

本案分析：

  • 关于利息：农场净收入（$25,000）足以支付利息。因此，遗孀必须支付利息。
  • 关于本金：本金是对财产资本价值的偿还，受益人是未来的所有者。因此，三个子女作为剩余权人，必须分摊本金的支付。
  • 关于个人责任 (Personal Liability)：女儿并没有签署借据（Note），她是因继承而获得财产权益。因此，她不需要对债务承担个人责任（即银行不能直接起诉她要求用她的私房钱还债）。
  • 关于止赎风险 (Foreclosure)：虽然她没有个人责任，但按揭是附着在土地上的担保物权。如果本金没人支付，银行会取消抵押品赎回权（Foreclosure），导致土地被拍卖。为了保住她未来的那份财产，她必须出钱支付本金。

因此，选项 C 准确描述了她的处境：无个人责任，但面临丧失财产权益的风险。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 A (分割诉讼 Partition)：
通常，分割诉讼仅适用于同时拥有权益的人（如按份共有人 Tenants in Common）。终身地产权人和剩余权人是连续拥有权益，大多数司法管辖区不允许剩余权人强迫出售终身地产权人的权益。

❌ 选项 B (强制个人支付)：
如前所述，除非女儿签署了贷款协议或承担了债务，否则她不对死者的债务承担个人责任 (Personal Liability)。她的风险仅限于失去该继承的财产。

❌ 选项 D (强制遗孀支付本金)：
这是一个常见的干扰项。虽然遗孀收入很高（$25,000），但这只增加了她支付利息的能力。无论收入多高，终身地产权人通常都没有义务支付本金，因为那是为了增加剩余权人的资产价值。

💡 MBE 考试技巧
记住口诀：
"Life Tenant pays Interest (Current Benefit)"
"Remainderman pays Principal (Future Corpus)"
如果题目问及责任，先看是本金还是利息！

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
By deed, a landowner conveyed land to a charity "on the condition that the land be used as a wildlife refuge, and if not, the landowner and his heirs may enter and terminate the estate hereby created." The following year the landowner died. His sister was his sole heir. By will, the landowner devised "all of my real property interests to my friend." One year after the landowner's death, the sister, by quitclaim deed, conveyed any interest she had in the land to a developer. Two years after the landowner's death, the landowner's sister died. Her sole heir was her husband. Recently, three years after the landowner's death, the charity ceased to use the land as a wildlife refuge.
Who may properly bring an action against the charity to recover fee simple ownership of the land?

choices.A: The developer.
choices.B: The landowner's friend.
choices.C: The sister's husband.
choices.D: No one.

questions.explanation:
Landowner
FSSCS
“to the charity on the condition that if the land is not used as a wildlife refuge”
Right of entry
“the landowner and his heirs may enter and terminate the estate”
Devise
“devised all of my real property interests to my friend”
FSSCS = Fee simple subject to condition subsequent.

A fee simple subject to a condition subsequent (FSSCS) is created through specific conditional language, such as “but if” or “on the condition that.” Upon the occurrence of the condition, the grantor (or his/her successor in interest) has the right to enter and terminate the estate if the grantor explicitly retained this right of entry† in the conveyance. The right of entry is fully transferable upon death – meaning that it is devisable by will or descendible through intestate succession – but in most states it is not alienable during life.

Here, the landowner conveyed an FSSCS to the charity and retained a right of entry that could be exercised if the land was no longer used as a wildlife refuge. The landowner then devised all of his real property interests – including the right of entry – to his friend. And since the charity recently ceased to use the land as a wildlife refuge, the friend can exercise the right of entry and bring an action to recover ownership of the land (Choice D).

†This right is also known as the “power of termination” or the “right of reentry.”

(Choices A & C) The landowner devised all of his real property interests to the friend, leaving no interest in the land for the sister to inherit upon his death. Because the sister had no interest in the land to convey to the developer by quitclaim deed or for her husband to inherit upon her death, neither of them may bring an action to recover ownership of the land from the charity.

📌 Educational Objective

The grantor of a fee simple subject to a condition subsequent can explicitly retain a right of entry, which allows the grantor (or his/her successor in interest) to enter and terminate the estate if the stated condition occurs. This right is devisable by will and descendible through intestate succession.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 45 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (fee simple subject to a condition subsequent).
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 155 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (power of termination or right of entry).
questions.zh-question:
一位土地所有者通过契据将土地转让给一个慈善机构，“条件是该土地被用作野生动物庇护所，否则，该土地所有者及其继承人可以进入并终止由此设立的地产权。”次年，该土地所有者去世。他的妹妹是其唯一继承人。通过遗嘱，该土地所有者将“我所有的不动产权益”遗赠给了他的朋友。在土地所有者去世一年后，其妹妹通过免责契据，将其在该土地上拥有的任何权益转让给了一位开发商。在土地所有者去世两年后，其妹妹去世。她的唯一继承人是她的丈夫。最近，在土地所有者去世三年后，该慈善机构停止将该土地用作野生动物庇护所。

谁可以合法地对该慈善机构提起诉讼，以收回该土地的完全保有产权（fee simple ownership）？

zh-choices.A: 该开发商。
zh-choices.B: 该土地所有者的朋友。
zh-choices.C: 该妹妹的丈夫。
zh-choices.D: 无人可以。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Real Property / Future Interests
正确答案：B

该土地所有者的朋友 (The landowner's friend)

本题考察的核心是未来权益的分类及其可转让性（特别是通过遗嘱转让）。

1. 核心法律概念
附带后决条件的可废止完全保有产权 (Fee Simple Subject to a Condition Subsequent, FSSCS)

当转让文书使用条件性语言（如 "on the condition that", "but if"）并明确保留进入权时设立。如果条件被违反，产权不会自动终止，而是赋予原所有人采取行动收回产权的权利。

进入权 / 终止权 (Right of Entry / Power of Termination)

这是 FSSCS 对应的未来权益。在现代法律和 MBE 考试中，这种权利是：

  • 可继承 (Descendible)： 若无遗嘱，传给法定继承人。
  • 可遗赠 (Devisable)： 可通过遗嘱传给受遗赠人。
  • 注意：在许多州，它在生前 (Inter Vivos) 不可转让，但本题不涉及生前转让。
2. 案情逐步推演
第一步：确定权益类型
土地所有者 (Landowner) 使用了 "on the condition that... enter and terminate" 的语言。
→ 慈善机构持有 FSSCS。
→ 土地所有者保留了 Right of Entry。
第二步：权益的转移 (关键点)
土地所有者去世并留有遗嘱 (Will)。遗嘱中将“所有不动产权益”赠予朋友 (Friend)。
→ Right of Entry 属于不动产权益，因此通过遗嘱转移给了朋友。
第三步：排除其他干扰项
由于遗嘱有效，土地所有者的妹妹 (Sister) 作为法定继承人 (Heir) 没有继承到任何权益。
→ 既然妹妹没有权益，她转让给开发商 (Developer) 的免责契据 (Quitclaim Deed) 也是无效的（或者说转让了“空”的权益）。
→ 妹妹的丈夫 (Husband) 同样无法从妹妹那里继承该权益。
第四步：条件的触发
慈善机构停止将土地用作野生动物庇护所。
→ 朋友作为 Right of Entry 的当前持有人，有权行使该权利并起诉收回土地。
⚠️ 常见陷阱： 考生容易混淆“法定继承人 (Heir)”和“受遗赠人 (Devisee)”。虽然题目提到妹妹是唯一继承人，但遗嘱 (Will) 的效力优先于无遗嘱继承 (Intestacy)。只要权益是可遗赠的（Right of Entry 是可遗赠的），它就会随遗嘱走，而不是随血缘走。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
看到 "on the condition that" 立即联想 Right of Entry。
看到 "so long as" 立即联想 Possibility of Reverter (自动回归)。

对于 Right of Entry，记住口诀："Willable but not always Saleable"（可立遗嘱传，但不一定能生前卖）。本题考的就是 "Willable" 这一点。
MBE Property Law Review

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A borrower, who is a citizen of State A, defaults on a loan secured by a mortgage on undeveloped land located in State B. The borrower executed the loan in State B and regularly transacts business there. The lender, who is a citizen of State B, sues the borrower in a state court in State A for the outstanding loan obligation before seeking to foreclose on the property. Under the laws of State A, a lender may sue the borrower directly on the debt before foreclosing on mortgaged property. Under the laws of State B, a lender must foreclose on the property before suing the borrower.
The court in State A determines that the conflict-of-laws rules of its own state should apply and that, under those rules, State B has the most significant relationship to the loan, the lender, and the borrower.
Should the court apply State A law or State B law regarding the lender's right to sue the borrower directly on the outstanding debt?

choices.A: State A law, because the borrower is a citizen of State A.
choices.B: State A law, because the court is located in State A.
choices.C: State B law, because State B has the most significant relationship to this matter.
choices.D: State B law, because the loan was originated in State B.

questions.explanation:
Conflict-of-laws rule for real property issues
General rule In cases involving real property, law applied by forum court should be determined by conflict-of-laws rule that would be applied by state where property is located
Exceptions
  • Document specifies application of specific jurisdiction's laws
  • Issues regarding effect of marriage on interest in land
  • Collateral issues (eg, whether transferor perpetrated fraud)
  • Issues regarding mortgage note (eg, validity of note)
  • Foreclosure-related issues that do not affect interest in land (eg, mortgagee's right to sue mortgagor for underlying debt before foreclosure)

Conflict-of-laws issues arise when significant aspects of a legal action are divided between two or more states, creating a conflict as to which state's law applies (as seen here). If the conflict involves real property, the general rule is that the law applied by the forum court should be determined by the conflict-of-laws rule that would be applied by the courts of the situs state—ie, the state where the property is located. Usually, the conflict-of-laws rule of the situs state calls for the application of its own local law on that issue (ie, the law of the situs).

However, this general rule does not apply to issues that are related to foreclosure but do not affect an interest in land—eg, a lender's right to sue a borrower on the outstanding debt before foreclosure (as seen here). Instead, such issues are determined by the law that governs the debt for which the mortgage was given, which is the law of the state that has the most significant relationship to the transaction and the parties (here, State B).

(Choice A) The borrower is a citizen of State A, so the State A court has personal jurisdiction over the borrower. But this does not mean that the State A court should apply State A law regarding the lender's right to sue the borrower before foreclosing on the mortgaged property.

(Choices B & D) Although the court is located in State A and the loan was originated in State B, the dispositive factor is which state has the most significant relationship to the issue at hand.

📌 Educational Objective

Issues that relate to foreclosure but do not affect an interest in land—eg, a lender's right to sue the borrower before foreclosing on the mortgaged property—are determined by the law of the state with the most significant relationship to the transaction and the parties.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws § 223, cmt. i (Am. Law Inst. 1971) (validity and effect of conveyance of interest in land).
questions.zh-question:
一名借款人，其为A州的公民，对一笔以位于B州的未开发土地的抵押权作担保的贷款违约。该借款人在B州签订了该贷款合同，并常于该地进行商业交易。贷款人是B州的公民，在寻求对该财产进行止赎之前，于A州的一家州法院就未偿还的贷款债务起诉了该借款人。根据A州的法律，贷款人可以在对抵押财产进行止赎前，直接就该债务起诉借款人。根据B州的法律，贷款人必须在起诉借款人之前先对该财产进行止赎。

A州的法院认定，应适用其本州的法律冲突规则，并且根据这些规则，B州与该贷款、贷款人和借款人具有最密切的联系。

关于贷款人是否有权就未偿还的债务直接起诉借款人这一问题，法院应适用A州法律还是B州法律？

zh-choices.A: A州法律，因为借款人是A州的公民。
zh-choices.B: A州法律，因为法院位于A州。
zh-choices.C: B州法律，因为B州与此案具有最密切的联系。
zh-choices.D: B州法律，因为该财产位于B州。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：不动产与法律冲突

本题考查的是法律冲突（Conflict of Laws）在涉及不动产抵押贷款交易中的具体应用。核心在于区分“对土地的权益”与“合同债务关系”。

核心法律规则

在处理涉及多个州的法律问题时，法院通常遵循以下原则：

  • 不动产权益 (Interest in Land)：通常适用物之所在地法 (Law of the Situs)。例如：抵押权的有效性、止赎的程序、土地所有权的转移。
  • 合同/债务问题 (Contract/Debt Issues)：对于不直接影响土地产权的附带问题（如本题中“能否直接起诉债务”），通常适用与交易和当事人有最密切联系 (Most Significant Relationship) 的州的法律。

题目分析逻辑

1 识别争议点：

本案的争议不是“谁拥有土地”或“抵押是否有效”，而是“贷款人能否在止赎前直接起诉借款人追讨债务”。这是一个关于借贷合同执行顺序的问题，属于债务/合同范畴，而非纯粹的土地产权范畴。

2 法院的认定：

题目明确指出，A州法院（法院地）决定适用其本州的法律冲突规则。根据该规则，法院已经认定：B州与该贷款、贷款人和借款人具有最密切的联系。

3 得出结论：

既然A州法院的冲突法规则指向“最密切联系地法”，且法院已认定B州为最密切联系地，那么就应当适用B州的法律。

✅ 正确答案：选项 C (State B law)

因为根据A州法院适用的“最密切联系原则”，B州是关系最密切的州，所以应适用B州法律（即必须先止赎，后起诉）。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • ❌ 选项 A (A州法律，因借款人是A州公民)：
    公民身份（Citizenship）确实影响法院的管辖权（Jurisdiction），但它不是决定适用哪州法律（Choice of Law）的唯一或主要因素。
  • ❌ 选项 B (A州法律，因法院在A州)：
    这混淆了“法院地法” (Lex Fori) 和法律选择规则。虽然A州法院审理此案，但A州的冲突法规则可能（且通常会）指引法院适用其他州的实体法。
  • ❌ 选项 D (B州法律，因财产在B州)：
    虽然结论也是适用B州法律，但理由不准确。
    如果是关于土地所有权的问题，理由确实应该是“财产所在地”。但本题是关于“债务起诉权”，其适用B州法律的根本原因是B州与交易有最密切联系（尽管财产所在地是建立这种联系的重要因素之一，但不是唯一的法律依据）。MBE考试中，推理过程与结论同样重要。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到涉及抵押（Mortgage）的法律冲突题时，请务必区分：

  1. 涉及土地本身的问题（如止赎方式、产权登记）：适用 Situs（所在地法）。
  2. 涉及底层债务/票据的问题（如票据有效性、起诉权、高利贷）：适用 Most Significant Relationship（最密切联系地法）。

本题中，题目已经帮你完成了“最密切联系地”的分析工作，直接顺着法院的认定选择对应的法律即可。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman died and in her duly probated will devised a tract of land to her son "for life" and then to "the heirs of his body in fee simple absolute." The son used the tract to secure a loan from a bank. When the son defaulted on the debt, the bank initiated foreclosure proceedings. A buyer acquired the tract at the foreclosure sale and promptly sold the tract to a friend. Both the buyer's deed and the friend's deed referenced the woman's will for the description of the parcel, and both deeds were promptly recorded.
Twenty years later, the son died intestate, leaving two children as his only heirs. The children have sued the friend, claiming ownership of the land under a 30-year marketable title act.
If common law rules have not been modified in the jurisdiction, who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The children, because the friend acquired the son's life estate, which terminated when the son died.
choices.B: The children, because the friend's deed referenced the woman's will, which served as a notice of claim under the marketable title act.
choices.C: The friend, because the children failed to record a notice of claim.
choices.D: The friend, because the friend acquired the son's interest in fee simple absolute.

questions.explanation:
Woman
“to my son for life”
Life estate to son
“then to the heirs of his body in fee simple absolute”
Remainder to son (Rule in Shelley’s Case)
Son Fee simple absolute (Merger rule)
Son Fee simple absolute
foreclosure
Buyer Fee simple absolute
Friend Fee simple absolute

Under the common law, the Rule in Shelley’s Case applies when an instrument grants:

  • a freehold estate (eg, life estate) to a person and
  • a remainder to the same person’s heirs or the heirs of that person’s body.

When this occurs, that person is considered to hold the freehold estate AND the remainder, so the person’s heirs take nothing under the granting instrument. And under the doctrine of merger, if there is no intervening interest, the freehold estate and the remainder merge so that the person takes in fee simple absolute (FSA).

Here, the woman’s will devised a life estate to the son and the remainder to the heirs of his body. The son is therefore considered to hold the life estate and the remainder. Since there is no intervening interest (eg, had another life estate followed the son’s life estate), the son’s interests merged into an FSA that the buyer acquired at the foreclosure sale and subsequently conveyed to the friend. Therefore, the friend will likely prevail.

Had this jurisdiction abolished the Rule in Shelley’s Case (as most others have done), the parties would have taken the freehold estate and remainder in accordance with the language in the deed. This means that the son would have received a life estate—subsequently acquired by the buyer and then the friend—that would have terminated upon the son’s death. And the children would have received the remainder and therefore prevailed (Choice A).

(Choices B & C) Marketable title acts extinguish any title defects that have not been recorded within the statutory period (here, 30 years). Since the buyer’s and friend’s recorded deeds referenced the granting language from the woman’s will, this likely satisfied the act’s recording requirement. However, the children still have no claim to enforce.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the Rule in Shelley’s Case, an instrument that grants a freehold estate to a person and a remainder to that same person’s heirs gives that person both interests. If there is no intervening interest, then the merger rule consolidates those interests into a fee simple absolute.
questions.zh-question:
一名女性去世，在其经正式遗嘱认证的遗嘱中，她将一块土地遗赠给她的儿子“终身”，然后遗赠给“其直系血亲继承人，以绝对无条件继承方式”。儿子用这块土地向银行申请贷款作为担保。当儿子拖欠债务时，银行启动了止赎程序。一名买方在止赎拍卖中购得该土地，并迅速将土地出售给一位朋友。买方的地契和朋友的地契在描述地块时都引用了该女性的遗嘱，并且两份地契都已及时登记。

二十年后，儿子未立遗嘱而亡，留下两个孩子作为其唯一继承人。孩子们根据一项30年的可售卖产权法起诉了这位朋友，主张土地的所有权。

如果该司法管辖区的普通法规则未被修改，谁可能会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 孩子们，因为朋友获得的是儿子的终身地产权，该权利在儿子去世时即告终止。
zh-choices.B: 孩子们，因为朋友的地契引用了该女性的遗嘱，这根据可售卖产权法构成了权利主张的通知。
zh-choices.C: 朋友，因为孩子们未能登记权利主张通知。
zh-choices.D: 朋友，因为朋友获得的是儿子在绝对无条件继承下的权益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Future Interests
正确答案：D

朋友胜诉，因为他获得了绝对无条件继承权 (Fee Simple Absolute)。

核心法律原则

本题的关键在于题目明确指出“普通法规则未被修改” (Common law rules have not been modified)。这触发了古老的财产法规则：

  • 1
    雪莱案规则 (Rule in Shelley's Case)
    如果一份文书将土地授予某人（A）终身，并将剩余地产权授予A的继承人 (A's Heirs)，普通法强制将该剩余地产权授予A本人，而不是A的继承人。
  • 2
    合并原则 (Doctrine of Merger)
    如果同一个人持有现在的终身地产权 (Life Estate) 和紧随其后的既得剩余地产权 (Vested Remainder)，这两个权益会合并。
本案逻辑推演
遗嘱措辞：
"To Son for life" + "To heirs of his body"
↓
应用雪莱案规则：
"Heirs" 的权益变成了 Son 的权益
Son 拥有：Life Estate + Remainder
↓
应用合并原则：
Life Estate + Remainder = Fee Simple Absolute

结论：

当遗嘱生效时，儿子实际上获得了这块土地的完整所有权 (Fee Simple Absolute)。因此：

  1. 儿子向银行抵押的是完整所有权。
  2. 银行止赎并卖给买方的是完整所有权。
  3. 朋友从买方手中买到的也是完整所有权。
  4. 儿子去世时，他的孩子们没有任何剩余权益，因为该权益早在几十年前就已经“合并”给了儿子并被卖掉了。
干扰项排除

选项 A (Children prevail):
这是现代法律（废除雪莱案规则后）的结果。但题目特意强调适用“未修改的普通法”，因此不能选此项。

选项 B & C (Marketable Title Act):
这是干扰项（Red Herring）。可售卖产权法 (Marketable Title Act) 旨在清除陈旧的产权瑕疵，但它不能创造权益。由于根据普通法，孩子们从一开始就没有获得任何权益（权益归父亲所有），无论是否登记，他们都没有权利主张。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到 "Common Law" 字眼时要警惕！
现代财产法大多已废除了 Rule in Shelley's Case 和 Doctrine of Worthier Title。但如果 MBE 题目设定在“普通法管辖区”，你必须应用这些古老的规则。这些规则通常会挫败授予人的意图（即本想给孩子留地，结果被父亲卖掉了）。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An individual devised a wooded parcel of land to her two children, a daughter and a son, with the daughter being given a 75 percent interest in the land and the son a 25 percent interest. The daughter intends to harvest timber from the land without seeking permission from her brother, whom she knows would object to altering the parcel from its natural state.
How much of the timber on the land is the daughter entitled to harvest?

choices.A: All of the timber, because a cotenant is entitled to all of the natural resources on the co-owned land.
choices.B: Seventy-five percent, because the daughter is only entitled to the share of natural resources that corresponds with her ownership interest in the land.
choices.C: Fifty percent, because the daughter is a tenant in common.
choices.D: None, unless the brother consents.

questions.explanation:
Rights & duties of cotenants
Rights
  • Possess & enjoy entire property
  • Receive proportionate shares of net profits from removal of natural resources
  • Receive pro rata shares of rent from third parties
Duties
  • Pay proportionate shares of expenses that may give rise to lien (eg, mortgage, property tax)
  • Contribute to repair or improvement costs, but only upon agreement

A concurrent estate (ie, cotenancy ) arises when two or more persons own real property at the same time. In any cotenancy, the cotenants have certain rights and duties — including the right to possess the entire property, regardless of the size of their ownership interests. However, each cotenant's right to natural resources found on the land (eg, minerals, oil, gas, timber — as seen here) is limited to the size of the cotenant's interest in the land (Choice A).

Here, the son and the daughter are cotenants with respect to the wooded parcel of land. The daughter's share of the cotenancy is 75 percent, so she is entitled to harvest 75 percent of the timber on the land — regardless of whether her brother consents (Choice D).

(Choice C) The daughter and the son have a tenancy in common, as evidenced by the fact that they did not take the land in equal shares. But the daughter is entitled to harvest 75 percent of the timber (not 50 percent) because that is the size of her ownership interest.

📌 Educational Objective

Each cotenant's right to natural resources on the land (eg, timber) is limited to the size of the cotenant's ownership interest.

📚 References
  • 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 43 (2020) (use and enjoyment—timber).

一个人将一块林地遗赠给她的两个孩子，一个女儿和一个儿子，其中女儿获得了该土地75%的权益，儿子获得了25%的权益。

女儿打算未经其兄弟许可，采伐这片土地上的木材。

女儿有权采伐这片土地上多少木材？

zh-choices.A: 所有的木材，因为土地的共有人有权获得该土地上的所有自然资源。
zh-choices.B: 百分之七十五，因为这个数量与她在这片土地上的所有权权益相对应。
zh-choices.C: 百分之五十，因为她是按份共有人（tenant in common）。
zh-choices.D: 一点也不能，除非她的兄弟同意。

questions.zh-explanation:
Real Property Cotenancy

MBE 考点解析：共有人的自然资源权利

本题考察的核心法律概念是按份共有（Tenancy in Common）下，共有人对土地上自然资源（Natural Resources）的权利范围。

正确答案：B
女儿有权采伐 75% 的木材，因为这与她的所有权权益比例相符。

1. 核心法律规则 (The Rule)

在处理共有财产（Concurrent Estates）时，MBE 经常考察“占有权”与“资源开采权”的区别：

占有权 (Possession) 每个共有人，无论其份额大小（哪怕只有1%），都有权占有和使用整个不动产。
自然资源 (Natural Resources) 对于会消耗土地价值的资源（如木材 Timber、矿产 Minerals、石油 Oil & Gas），共有人的权利受限于其所有权份额（Interest Share）。

2. 案情分析与逻辑推理

法律关系认定：
题目中母亲将土地留给子女，且份额不均等（75% vs 25%）。这构成了按份共有（Tenancy in Common）。按份共有不要求份额均等。

为何选 B (75%)：

  • 虽然女儿有权“进入”并“占有”整块土地，但采伐木材属于对土地本体的消耗。
  • 如果她采伐超过 75% 的木材，她就侵犯了儿子的财产权益，可能构成毁损（Waste）。
  • 因此，她单方面有权处置的资源上限，就是她所持有的权益比例（75%）。

3. 排除错误选项

  • 选项 A (100%) 错误： 虽然共有人可以占有整块土地，但不能独吞所有资源。如果她拿走所有木材，她必须向兄弟进行账目核算（Accounting），支付多拿部分的收益。
  • 选项 C (50%) 错误： 这是对“按份共有”的误解。只有在未指明份额时，法律才推定为均等。本题明确规定了 75/25 的比例，权利随比例而定。
  • 选项 D (需同意) 错误： 共有人行使权利通常不需要其他共有人的同意（Consent）。她可以在自己的份额范围内自由行动。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在做 Cotenancy（共有）题目时，请务必区分以下两种情况：

  1. 使用（Use/Possession）： 住在房子里、在草地上散步 → 每个人都有权使用 100% 的区域，无需支付租金（除非有 ouster）。
  2. 消耗/获利（Depletion/Profits）： 挖矿、砍树、出租给第三方 → 必须按份额比例分配收益或受限于份额上限。

本题属于第二种情况。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned in fee simple Lots 1 and 2 in an urban subdivision. The lots were vacant and unproductive. They were held as a speculation that their value would increase. The man died and, by his duly probated will, devised the residue of his estate (of which Lots 1 and 2 were part) to his wife for life with remainder in fee simple to his sister. The man's executor distributed the estate under appropriate court order and notified the wife that future real estate taxes on Lots 1 and 2 were her responsibility to pay.
Except for the statutes relating to probate and those relating to real estate taxes, there is no applicable statute.
The wife left the lots vacant and did not pay the real estate taxes due for Lots 1 and 2. To prevent a tax sale of the fee simple, the sister paid the taxes and demanded that the wife reimburse her for same. When the wife refused, the sister brought an appropriate action against the wife to recover the amount paid.
In such action, what should the sister recover?

choices.A: Nothing, because the wife never received any income from the lots.
choices.B: Nothing, because the wife's sole possession gave the right to decide whether or not taxes should be paid.
choices.C: The amount paid, because a life tenant has the duty to pay current charges.
choices.D: The present value of the interest that the amount paid would earn during the wife's lifetime.

questions.explanation:
Life tenant's duties
Duty to pay current charges Life tenant must pay all current charges due during life tenancy (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest) up to financial benefit received from property
Duty to prevent waste Life tenant must prevent affirmative waste (ie, voluntary waste), permissive waste & ameliorative waste
Duty to make ordinary repairs Life tenant must make reasonable repairs to preserve property

The holder of a life estate (ie, the life tenant) has a duty to pay current charges on the land that become due during the life tenancy (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest). But this duty is limited to the financial benefit that the life tenant receives from the property. Therefore, there is no duty to pay these charges if the life tenant is not in possession of the property and does not receive rent or other income from the property.

Here, the man's wife received a life estate ("to his wife for life") and the remainder was owned by his sister ("remainder in fee simple to his sister"). Although a life tenant generally has the duty to pay real estate taxes, the lots were left vacant and unproductive. As a result, the wife received no financial benefit from the lots and had no duty to pay the real estate taxes. The sister should therefore recover nothing.

(Choice B) The wife's duty to pay taxes depends on the financial benefit she received from the land, not merely her possession of it.

(Choices C & D) Had the wife been obligated to pay the real estate taxes, the sister could have recovered the amount paid and possibly the interest that accrued during the repayment period (but not during the wife's lifetime).

📌 Educational Objective

A life tenant's duty to pay current charges on the land is limited to the financial benefit that the life tenant receives from the property. Therefore, this duty is not owed if the life tenant is not in possession of and receives no income from the property.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property §§ 129–130 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (duty to pay current charges).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子以完全保有地权的形式拥有城市分区中的地块1（Lot 1）和地块2（Lot 2）。这些地块空置且无产出，被持有用于投机，期望其价值会上涨。该男子去世，通过其经正式遗嘱检验的遗嘱，将其剩余遗产（包括地块1和地块2）遗赠给其妻子，授予其终身保有权，剩余权益则以完全保有地权的形式遗赠给其妹妹。该男子的遗嘱执行人根据适当的法院命令分配了遗产，并通知其妻子，地块1和地块2未来的房产税应由她负责支付。

除与遗嘱检验和房产税相关的法规外，没有其他适用的法规。

妻子让这些地块保持空置，并且没有支付地块1和地块2到期的房产税。为防止该完全保有地权因欠税被出售，妹妹支付了税款，并要求妻子偿还该笔款项。当妻子拒绝后，妹妹对妻子提起了适当的诉讼，以追回其支付的款项。

在此诉讼中，妹妹应能获得多少赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 无，因为妻子从未从这些地块中获得任何收入。
zh-choices.B: 无，因为妻子的单独占有权使其有权决定是否应支付税款。
zh-choices.C: 支付的金额，因为终身保有人有责任支付当期费用。
zh-choices.D: 在妻子有生之年，已支付金额所能产生的利息的现值。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Life Estates & Duties
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (Black Letter Law)

终身保有人 (Life Tenant) 有义务支付房产的当期费用（如房产税、抵押贷款利息），但这并非绝对义务。该义务有一个上限 (Cap)：

  • 仅限于终身保有人从该房产获得的经济利益 (Financial Benefit)。

案例分析逻辑

1 一般原则：
通常情况下，终身保有人必须支付房产税，以防止产生“容许损耗”(Permissive Waste)。如果他不支付，剩余权益持有人 (Remainderman) 可以支付并要求偿还。
2 责任的限制（关键点）：
支付责任的金额上限取决于房产的使用情况：
  • 若房产产生收入：上限为总收入 (Gross Income)。
  • 若房产自住（无收入）：上限为公平租金价值 (Fair Rental Value)。
  • 若房产空置且无产出：上限为 0。
3 代入本题事实：
题目明确指出地块是“空置且无产出的” (vacant and unproductive)，且妻子“从未获得任何收入”。

结论： 妻子的经济收益为 $0，因此她支付房产税的义务上限也是 $0。
✅ 正确答案：A
无，因为妻子从未从这些地块中获得任何收入。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 B (占有权决定论)：
错误。虽然妻子有占有权 (Right to Possession)，但这并不赋予她随意决定不交税的权利。她不交税的原因是因为没有收益，而不是因为她拥有占有权。
❌ 选项 C (绝对责任论)：
错误。这是最具迷惑性的选项。它陈述了一般规则（终身保有人需支付费用），但忽略了“以经济收益为限”这一关键的例外情况。
❌ 选项 D (现值计算)：
错误。既然妻子没有支付义务，计算赔偿金额的方法就无关紧要了。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Six years ago, the owner of an estate in fee simple executed and delivered to his nephew an instrument in the proper form of a warranty deed, purporting to convey his estate to "my nephew and his heirs." At that time, the nephew was a widower who had one child, a daughter.
Three years ago, the nephew executed and delivered to his neighbor an instrument in the proper form of a warranty deed, purporting to convey the estate to "my neighbor." The nephew's daughter did not join in the deed. The neighbor was, and still is, unmarried and childless.
The only possibly applicable statute in the jurisdiction states that any deed will be construed to convey the grantor's entire estate, unless expressly limited.
Last month, the nephew died, never having remarried. His daughter is his only heir.
Who is the owner of the estate?

choices.A: The daughter and neighbor as joint tenants, because both survived the nephew.
choices.B: The daughter and neighbor as tenants in common of equal shares.
choices.C: The daughter, because the nephew's death ended the neighbor's life estate pur autre vie.
choices.D: The neighbor in fee simple pursuant to the nephew's deed.

questions.explanation:
Conveying fee simple absolute

Owner
“to my nephew and his heirs”
words of purchase
words of limitation
words of purchase + words of limitation = express fee simple absolute
Nephew
“to my neighbor”
words of purchase
words of purchase – words of limitation = presumed fee simple absolute
Neighbor

Ownership in real property is transferred from a grantor (current owner) to a grantee (new owner) through a conveying instrument like a will or deed. A conveying instrument usually contains both:

  • words of purchase – identifying the new owner (eg, “to my nephew”)
  • words of limitation – identifying the type of estate being conveyed (eg, “and his heirs”).

“And his/her heirs” are words of limitation traditionally used to transfer a fee simple absolute (FSA or fee simple) – the most common and broadest form of property ownership. However, these words of limitation are not required since an FSA is presumed by law when no such words are used. And since an FSA conveys title without any conditions, limitations, or accompanying future interests, no ownership interest is created in the grantee's heirs.

Here, the owner of an FSA conveyed his interest to his nephew by warranty deed. Since the deed used the words of limitation “and his heirs,” it conveyed an FSA to the nephew (but created no ownership interest in the daughter/heir). The nephew then conveyed his interest to his neighbor by a warranty deed that lacked words of limitation. Therefore, the neighbor received an FSA and owns the estate without any conditions or limitations.

(Choices A & B) Joint tenancy and tenancy in common are two types of concurrent estates. Concurrent estates are created only when a conveying instrument identifies two or more persons as grantees (not seen here).

(Choice C) A life estate pur autre vie is an ownership interest that lasts for the duration of the life of someone other than the grantee. It is transferred when a conveying instrument states “to A” (words of purchase) “for the life of B” (words of limitation). Since the nephew's warranty deed to the neighbor contained no such language, the neighbor did not receive a life estate pur autre vie.

📌 Educational Objective

A fee simple absolute is the broadest form of property ownership and is transferred when the conveying instrument's words of limitation state “and his/her heirs” OR when no words of limitation are used.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 14 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (types of fee simple estates).
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 15 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (estate in fee simple absolute).
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 39 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (presumption of fee simple absolute).
questions.zh-question:
六年前，一位完全保有地产权（fee simple）的所有人签署并向其侄子交付了一份格式合规的担保契据（warranty deed），意图将其地产转让给“我的侄子及其继承人”。当时，该侄子是鳏夫，有一个女儿。

三年前，该侄子签署并向其邻居交付了一份格式合规的担保契据，意图将该地产转让给“我的邻居”。侄子的女儿未在该契据上联署。该邻居当时至今均未婚且无子女。

该司法管辖区唯一可能适用的成文法规定，任何契据都将被解释为转让转让人的全部地产权，除非有明确限制。

上个月，侄子去世，未再婚。他的女儿是他唯一的继承人。

谁是该地产的所有人？

zh-choices.A: 女儿和邻居作为联权共有人（joint tenants），因为他们都在侄子去世后存活。
zh-choices.B: 女儿和邻居作为拥有同等份额的按份共有人（tenants in common）。
zh-choices.C: 女儿，因为侄子的死亡终止了邻居的他益终身地产权（life estate pur autre vie）。
zh-choices.D: 邻居，依据侄子的契据拥有完全保有地产权（fee simple）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Ownership
正确答案：D
邻居拥有完全保有地产权 (Fee Simple)
核心考点：受让人条款 vs. 权属限制条款

在普通法中，短语 "To A and his heirs" 包含两部分：

  • "To A"：受让人条款 (Words of Purchase)，指明谁获得土地。
  • "and his heirs"：权属限制条款 (Words of Limitation)，指明获得什么类型的权益（即 Fee Simple）。

关键点：这并不给继承人任何权益！

第一步：原房主 -> 侄子
契据写着 "to my nephew and his heirs"。
根据法律规则，这创造了 Fee Simple Absolute（绝对完全保有地产权）。
结果：侄子拥有房产的全部所有权。侄子的女儿（继承人）此时没有任何权益（No interest）。
第二步：侄子 -> 邻居
侄子将房产转让给 "my neighbor"。
题目中的法规指出：除非明确限制，否则视为转让全部权益。
结果：侄子将他拥有的 Fee Simple 全部转让给了邻居。
第三步：侄子去世
侄子去世时，他已经不再拥有该房产。
结果：作为继承人的女儿无法继承该房产，因为该房产已不属于侄子的遗产。
为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A & B (共有权):
共有权（Joint Tenancy 或 Tenancy in Common）需要同时转让给两个或以上的人。本案中从未出现同时转让给女儿和邻居的情况。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman died testate. In her will, she devised a farm she owned to her husband for life, remainder to her niece. Her will did not specify the duties of the husband and the niece with regard to maintenance and expenses related to the farm. The husband took sole possession of the farm, did not farm the land, and did not rent the land to a third person, although the fair rental value was substantial.
For two years in a row after the woman died, the county assessor sent the tax bills to the niece. However, the niece did not pay the bills, because she and the husband could not agree on who should pay them. Finally, the niece paid the taxes to avoid a tax foreclosure sale.
The niece then sued the husband for reimbursement for the two years' worth of property taxes.
There is no applicable statute.
Is the niece likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because remaindermen are solely responsible for the payment of property taxes.
choices.B: No, because the county assessor sent the bills to the niece.
choices.C: No, because the woman's will was silent on responsibility for payment of property taxes.
choices.D: Yes, because the niece paid an obligation that was the sole responsibility of the husband.

questions.explanation:
Life tenant's duties
Duty to pay current charges Life tenant must pay all current charges due during life tenancy (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest) up to financial benefit received from property
Duty to prevent waste Life tenant must prevent affirmative waste (ie, voluntary waste), permissive waste & ameliorative waste
Duty to make ordinary repairs Life tenant must make reasonable repairs to preserve property

The holder of a life estate (ie, the life tenant) has a duty to pay current charges - eg, property taxes and mortgage interest - unless the document creating the life estate provides otherwise. This duty is limited to the amount of income that can be generated from the land. If the holder of the remainder (ie, the remainderman) pays the current property charges instead, then the remainderman is entitled to reimbursement from the life tenant.

Here, the woman's will granted the husband a life estate but was silent regarding the duty to pay current charges. Therefore, the husband (life tenant) had a duty to pay those charges - including the property taxes - up to the amount of income the farm could generate. Because the farm's fair rental value was substantial, the husband was obligated to pay all the property taxes. But since the niece (remainderman) ultimately paid those taxes, she is entitled to reimbursement from the husband.

(Choices A & C) Life tenants - not remaindermen - are solely responsible for all current charges unless the document creating the life estate provides otherwise. Here, the woman's will was silent on the matter, so the property taxes were the husband's sole responsibility.

(Choice B) The fact that the county assessor sent the tax bills to the niece has no effect on the husband's obligation to pay or reimburse the property taxes.

📌 Educational Objective

Unless the document creating the life estate provides otherwise, a life tenant has the duty to pay all current charges (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest) up to the amount of income that can be generated from the land.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property §§ 129 - 130 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (life tenant's duty to pay current charges).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性立有遗嘱去世。在遗嘱中，她将自己拥有的一个农场遗赠给她的丈夫终身保有，剩余权益归于她的侄女。她的遗嘱没有具体说明丈夫和侄女在农场维护和费用方面的责任。丈夫取得了农场的独占权，但他没有耕种土地，也没有将土地出租给第三方，尽管其公允租金价值相当可观。

在该女性去世后的连续两年里，县税务评估员将税单寄给了侄女。然而，侄女没有支付这些账单，因为她和丈夫无法就谁应该支付达成一致。最终，为了避免税务止赎拍卖，侄女支付了税款。

随后，侄女起诉丈夫，要求其偿还这两年的房产税。

本案无适用的成文法。

侄女有可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为剩余权益人对支付房产税负有全部责任。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为县税务评估员将账单寄给了侄女。
zh-choices.C: 不会，因为该女性的遗嘱对支付房产税的责任未作规定。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为侄女支付了一项本应由丈夫承担全部责任的债务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Life Estates & Taxes
⚖️ 核心法律规则

本题考察的是终身保有人 (Life Tenant) 与剩余权益人 (Remainderman) 之间的责任分配。

默认规则 (Default Rule)：
除非遗嘱或契据另有规定，终身保有人有义务支付房产的当期费用 (Current Charges)，如房产税和抵押贷款利息。

但这个义务是有限额的 (Capped)：

  • 如果终身保有人自己居住/占有该房产：支付限额为该房产的公允租金价值 (Fair Rental Value)。
  • 如果终身保有人出租该房产：支付限额为实际收到的租金收入。
🔍 案情深度分析
1
角色定位：
丈夫是终身保有人 (Life Tenant)，侄女是剩余权益人 (Remainderman)。
2
遗嘱沉默 (Silence in Will)：
遗嘱未规定费用分摊，因此适用普通法默认规则：终身保有人负责支付房产税。
3
支付能力的界定 (The Cap)：
丈夫虽然没有耕种也没有出租，但他独占 (Sole Possession) 了农场。题目明确指出农场的公允租金价值 (Fair Rental Value) 相当可观 (Substantial)。
推论：由于公允租金价值足以覆盖房产税，丈夫作为终身保有人，对房产税负有全部责任。
✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 D)

侄女会胜诉。

因为根据法律，丈夫有义务支付房产税（属于防止放任损耗 Permissive Waste 的一种）。

侄女作为剩余权益人，为了保护自己的未来权益不被税务止赎 (Tax Foreclosure) 剥夺，被迫支付了这笔钱。这构成了一种代位求偿 (Subrogation) 或不当得利的情形，她有权要求丈夫偿还这笔本应由他承担的债务。

❌ 易错项排除
选项 A 错误：剩余权益人通常只负责支付抵押贷款的本金 (Principal) 部分，而不负责房产税等当期费用（除非费用超过了房产的收益/租金价值）。
选项 B 错误：税单寄给谁是行政程序问题，不改变法律上的纳税义务 (Legal Liability)。
选项 C 错误：遗嘱沉默并不意味着没人负责，而是意味着适用普通法的默认规则（即终身保有人负责）。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在处理 Life Estate 题目时，一定要检查房产是否产生收入或具有租金价值。

如果题目说这是一块“荒地”且“无租金价值”，那么终身保有人可能就不需要支付税款了。但本题强调了 "Substantial Fair Rental Value"，这就是在暗示你：钱够付税，必须付！

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Thirty years ago, a landowner conveyed land by warranty deed to a church (a charity) "so long as the land herein conveyed is used as the site for the principal religious edifice maintained by said church."
Twenty years ago, the landowner died intestate, survived by a single heir.
One year ago, the church dissolved and its church building situated on the land was demolished.
There is no applicable statute. The common law Rule Against Perpetuities is unmodified in the jurisdiction.
In an appropriate action, the landowner's heir and the attorney general, who is the appropriate official to assert public interests in charitable trusts, contest the right to the land.
In this action, who will prevail?

choices.A: The attorney general, because cy pres should be applied to devote the land to religious purposes to carry out the charitable intent of the landowner.
choices.B: The attorney general, because the landowner's attempt to restrict the church's fee simple violated the common law Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.C: The landowner's heir, as successor to the landowner's possibility of reverter.
choices.D: The landowner's heir, because a charity cannot convey assets donated to it.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible Fee simple determinable
  • Durational
    • “so long as”
    • “during”
    • “until”
Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest (ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Defeasible Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • Conditional
    • “but if”
    • “provided that”
    • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

Defeasible fees are fee simple estates that automatically terminate if a specified event or condition occurs. One type of defeasible fee is a fee simple determinable (FSD), which is created with durational language (eg, “so long as”). An FSD is followed by either:

  • a possibility of reverter – when the estate automatically reverts back to the grantor upon the happening of the specified event (presumed if not expressly stated) or
  • an executory interest – when the estate automatically passes to a third party upon the happening of the specified event (must be expressly stated).

Here, the landowner conveyed the church an FSD followed by the landowner’s possibility of reverter. When the landowner died, his possibility of reverter was inherited by his sole heir. So when the church dissolved and its principal religious edifice (ie, the church building) was demolished, title automatically reverted to the landowner’s heir. Therefore, the heir will prevail.

(Choice A) When a charitable trust no longer serves the purpose for which it was created, courts can use the cy pres doctrine to redirect the trust to a similar charity or purpose. However, this doctrine does not apply when the conveyance includes a possibility of reverter (as seen here) or otherwise dictates what should happen when the assets for the trust are no longer used.

(Choice B) Under the Rule Against Perpetuities, specific future interests are void if there is any possibility that the interest will not vest within 21 years after the end of all lives in being at the creation of the interest. But this rule does not apply to future interests held by the grantor (eg, a possibility of reverter) OR charitable trusts.

(Choice D) A charity can convey assets donated to it.

📌 Educational Objective

A fee simple determinable is a defeasible fee created with durational language. Unless otherwise stated, it is presumed that the estate will automatically revert back to the grantor if the terminating event or condition occurs.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 44 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (fee simple determinable).
questions.zh-question:
三十年前，一位土地所有者通过附有担保的契约将土地转让给一个教堂（一个慈善机构），契约规定“只要此转让的土地被用作所述教堂维持其主要宗教建筑的所在地”。

二十年前，该土地所有者未立遗嘱而去世，仅有一位继承人尚存。

一年前，该教堂解散，其位于该土地上的教堂建筑被拆除。

本案没有适用的成文法。在该司法管辖区内，普通法中的反永久所有权规则(Rule Against Perpetuities)未作修改。

在一项适当的诉讼中，土地所有者的继承人与司法部长（他是维护慈善信托公共利益的适当官员）就土地的权利展开争讼。

在这场诉讼中，谁将胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 司法部长，因为应适用近似适用原则(cy pres)，将土地用于宗教目的，以实现土地所有者的慈善意图。
zh-choices.B: 司法部长，因为土地所有者试图限制教堂的完全保有地产权(fee simple)的行为，违反了普通法中的反永久所有权规则(Rule Against Perpetuities)。
zh-choices.C: 土地所有者的继承人，作为土地所有者的复归可能性(possibility of reverter)的继承人。
zh-choices.D: 土地所有者的继承人，因为慈善机构不能转让捐赠给它的资产。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Future Interests
✅ 正确答案：选项 C

土地所有者的继承人胜诉。

因为该地产权在条件被违反时自动终止，所有权自动回到了继承人手中。

本题考察的核心是可废除的完全保有地产权 (Defeasible Fees) 的分类及其对应的未来权益 (Future Interests)。

1. 识别地产权类型

题目中的关键用语是：
"so long as..." (只要...)

这是典型的持续性用语 (Durational Language)。这种语言创造了：

Fee Simple Determinable (FSD)
可废止的完全保有地产权

法律后果：当特定条件（教堂不再作为主要宗教场所）发生时，该地产权自动 (Automatically) 终止。

2. 对应的未来权益

FSD 总是伴随着出让人（Grantor）保留的未来权益：

Possibility of Reverter
复归可能性

继承性：这种权益是可以继承的。当原土地所有者去世时，其继承人（Heir）继承了这一权益。一旦教堂拆除，条件触发，土地所有权自动复归给继承人。

3. 为什么不是其他选项？
争论点 法律规则解析
反永久所有权规则 (RAP)
(选项 B)		 RAP 不适用于出让人（Grantor）保留的权益（如 Possibility of Reverter）。它只限制给第三方的权益。因此，即使过了几百年，复归权依然有效。
近似适用原则 (Cy Pres)
(选项 A)		 Cy Pres 用于修正慈善信托以防止其失败。但在本案中，出让人设定了明确的复归机制。当特定地产权自动终止时，财产不再属于慈善机构，而是回到了私人手中，因此 Cy Pres 无从适用。
💡 MBE 拿分技巧

在看到 "So long as", "Until", "While" 等词汇时：

  1. 立即判定为 Fee Simple Determinable (FSD)。
  2. 记住口诀：FSD 自动结束 (Automatic Forfeiture)。
  3. 对应的未来权益是 Possibility of Reverter。
  4. 出让人的权益不受 RAP 限制。
MBE Real Property Review | © 2025 Exam Prep
